children.translated_text: He who has in every way destroyed all darkness, and lifted the world from the mire of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) —

children.text: tasmai namaskṛtya yathārthaśāstre śāstraṃ pravakṣyāmyabhidharmakośam // VAkK_1.1 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to that Teacher of truth, I shall expound the treatise, the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> (Treasury of <s>Abhidharma</s>).

children.text: prajñāmalā sānucarābhidharmaḥ tatprāptaye yāpi ca yacca śāstram /
children.translated_text: <s>Abhidharma</s> is stainless <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) together with its accompaniments; also that [practice] for attaining it, and the treatise [describing it].

children.text: tasyārthato 'smin samanupraveśāt sa cā śrayo 'syetyabhidharmakośam // VAkK_1.2 //
children.translated_text: Because there is entry into its meaning in this [treatise], and because it is the basis of that [<s>Abhidharma</s>], [this work is called] the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s> (Treasury of <s>Abhidharma</s>).

children.text: dharmāṇāṃ pravicayamantareṇa nāsti kleśānāṃ yata upaśāntaye 'bhyupāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without the thorough analysis of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), there is no means for the pacification of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions);

children.text: kleśaiśca bhramati bhavārṇave 'tra lokastaddhetorata uditaḥ kilaiṣa śāstrā // VAkK_1.3 //
children.translated_text: and it is because of afflictions that the world wanders in the ocean of existence — therefore, it is said, this treatise was proclaimed [by the Teacher].
Conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, excluding the path, are with-<s>āsravas</s> (with defilements) and without-<s>āsravas</s>;
they are 'with-<s>āsravas</s>' because the <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) 'lie alongside' them.
The without-<s>āsrava</s> [dharmas] are the truth of the path and also the threefold unconditioned.

children.text: ākāśaṃ dvau nirodhau ca tatrākāśamanāvṛtiḥ // VAkK_1.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) and the two cessations — of these, <s>ākāśa</s> is non-obstruction.
<s>Pratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (analytical cessation) is the disconnection [from afflictions], each one separately.
The other cessation, <s>apratisaṃkhyānirodha</s> (non-analytical cessation), is the absolute prevention of arising.
Those conditioned <s>dharmas</s>, moreover, are the five aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>): form (<s>rūpa</s>) and so forth.

children.text: sa evādhvā kathāvastu saniḥsārāḥ savastukāḥ // VAkK_1.7 //
children.translated_text: They are also the [three] times, the topics of discourse, [the dharmas] with outflows, and those with real existence.
Those that are with-<s>āsravas</s> are the aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandhas</s>), also called 'with going' [i.e., leading to rebirth].

children.text: duḥkhaṃ samudayo loko dṛṣṭisthānaṃ bhavaśca te // VAkK_1.8 //
children.translated_text: They are suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the origin (<s>samudaya</s>), 'the world' (<s>loka</s>), the basis for views (<s>dṛṣṭisthāna</s>), and existence (<s>bhava</s>).
<s>Rūpa</s> (form) consists of the five sense-faculties, the five sense-objects, and <s>avijñapti</s> (imperceptible form).
The bases of those [five] cognitions, the sensitive matter (<s>rūpaprasāda</s>) of the eye and the rest.
<s>Rūpa</s> (visible form) is twofold and twentyfold; sound is eightfold; taste
is sixfold; smell is fourfold; and the tangible is elevenfold in nature.
That which continues — whether wholesome or unwholesome — even for one whose mind is distracted,
based on the great elements, is called <s>avijñapti</s> (imperceptible form).
The [great] elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) are the elements of earth, water, fire, and wind.
They are established in the functions of supporting and so forth: hardness, moisture, heat, and movement.
Earth, in common parlance, refers to color and shape;

children.text: āpastejaśca vāyustu dhātureva tathāpi ca // VAkK_1.13 //
children.translated_text: water, fire, and wind [in common parlance] — but [in Abhidharma] it is the element itself that is meant.
The sense-faculties and sense-objects are held to be the ten <s>āyatanas</s> (bases) and <s>dhātus</s> (elements).
<s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) is experience; <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) has the nature of apprehending distinguishing marks.
The <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations) is other than those four [aggregates]; and these three [non-form aggregates]
are designated <s>dharmāyatana</s> and <s>dharmadhātu</s>, together with <s>avijñapti</s> and the unconditioned.

children.text: vijñānaṃ prativijñaptiḥ mana āyatanaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is awareness of each [object]; <s>manas</s> (mind) is also an <s>āyatana</s> (base);

children.text: dhātavaḥ sapta ca matāḥ ṣaḍ vijñānānyatho mahaḥ // VAkK_1.16 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) are considered to be seven [sense-consciousness elements]; the six consciousnesses, and also <s>manas</s>.
The immediately preceding and past consciousness of the six [consciousnesses] — that is <s>manas</s> (mind).
For the purpose of establishing the sixth sense-base, the eighteen <s>dhātus</s> are taught.
The complete inclusion of all [dharmas] is by means of one <s>skandha</s>, one <s>āyatana</s>,
and one <s>dhātu</s> — through [their] intrinsic nature and separation from the nature of others.
The unity of <s>dhātu</s> [is established] through birth, domain, cognition, and commonality;

children.text: dvitve 'pi cakṣurādīnāṃ śobhārtha tu dvayodbhavaḥ // VAkK_1.19 //
children.translated_text: even in [their] duality, the arising of the pair [object and consciousness] is for the purpose of clarity of the eye and the rest.
<s>Skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> mean 'heap,' 'gate,' and 'seed' respectively.
The three teachings of <s>skandhas</s> and so forth are due to delusion, [sharpness of] faculties, and preference, in three ways.
Because [feeling and perception] are the root of disputes and the cause of [continued] <s>saṃsāra</s>, and for the sake of sequence,
<s>vedanā</s> (feeling) and <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), from among the mental factors, are established as separate <s>skandhas</s>.
The unconditioned is not stated among the <s>skandhas</s>, because it does not apply; the sequence, moreover, [is determined]
by coarseness, defilement, [being a] vessel, and so forth — from the meaning of the <s>dhātus</s>.
The five [sense-objects are stated] first because they pertain to the present; the four [non-form skandhas] because they pertain to the material.
Otherwise the sequence is according to position, from the farther to the nearer in function.
For the purpose of specification, due to pre-eminence, multiplicity of <s>dharmas</s>, and inclusion of the foremost,
one <s>āyatana</s> is called '<s>rūpa</s>' and one is called '<s>dharma</s>.'
The eighty thousand collections of <s>Dharmaskandhas</s> (aggregates of <s>Dharma</s>) that the Sage proclaimed —
they are speech and name — their inclusion is within form and formations.
Some say the measure of the treatise [determines a <s>Dharmaskandha</s>]; the narrative of <s>skandhas</s> and so forth, one by one;
but the <s>Dharmaskandha</s> is explained as the antidote to a [particular type of] disposition.
Likewise other <s>skandhas</s>, <s>āyatanas</s>, and <s>dhātus</s> as appropriate
should be explained, having ascertained their specific characteristics according to what has been stated.
An opening [in matter] is called the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (space-element) — it is said to be [characterized by] light and darkness.
The <s>vijñānadhātu</s> (consciousness-element) is consciousness; with-<s>āsravas</s> [dharmas] are the basis of birth.
One [dhātu] here is 'with designation' — <s>rūpa</s> (visible form); ten are 'with resistance' (<s>sapratigha</s>) —

children.text: rūpiṇaḥ avyākṛtā aṣṭau ta evārūpaśabdakāḥ // VAkK_1.29 //
children.translated_text: the material [dhātus]; eight are indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — those same [ten] minus the immaterial and sound.
The others are threefold; all obtained in the desire-realm; in the form-realm, fourteen,
minus the elements of smell, taste, nose, tongue, and their respective consciousnesses.
In the formless realm, only the mind-element, dharma-element, and mind-consciousness-element are obtained;

children.text: sāsravānāsravā ete trayaḥ śeṣāstu sāsravāḥ // VAkK_1.31 //
children.translated_text: these three are both with-<s>āsravas</s> and without-<s>āsravas</s>; the rest are only with-<s>āsravas</s>.
The five consciousness-elements possess <s>vitarka</s> (initial application) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained application);
the last three are of three kinds; the rest are devoid of both.
Through the <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptualization) of examination and recollection, [dharmas are] non-conceptual;

children.text: tau prajñāmānasī vyagrā smṛtiḥ sarvaiva mānasī // VAkK_1.33 //
children.translated_text: those two [vitarka and vicāra] are, respectively, <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and mental [activity] that is active; <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is entirely mental.
Seven consciousness-<s>dhātus</s> have objects (<s>sālambana</s>); and half of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

children.text: navānupāttā te cāṣṭau śabdaśca anye nava dvidhā // VAkK_1.34 //
children.translated_text: Nine are 'not appropriated' (<s>anupātta</s>); those [nine] plus eight plus sound — the other nine are twofold.

children.text: spraṣṭavyaṃ dvividhaṃ śeṣā rūpiṇo nava bhautikāḥ /
children.translated_text: The tangible is twofold; the remaining nine material ones are derivative (<s>bhautika</s>).
A portion of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> [is also derivative]; of the ten material [dhātus], [some are] accumulated.

children.text: chinatti chidyate caiva bāhyaṃ dhātu catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: The external [material] group of four elements: cuts and is cut,
burns and weighs — thus there is a debate regarding the burner and the weigher.
The five internal [faculties] are of the nature of <s>vipāka</s> (karmic maturation) and <s>upacayika</s> (accumulative); the maturation-born,

children.text: na śabdaḥ apratighā aṣṭau naiḥṣyandika vipākajāḥ // VAkK_1.37 //
children.translated_text: but not sound; eight are without resistance; the outflowing [dharmas] are maturation-born.
The others are threefold; one possesses [real] substance; the last three are momentary.

children.text: cakṣurvijñānadhātvoḥ syāt pṛthak lābhaḥ sahāpi ca // VAkK_1.38 //
children.translated_text: The eye and eye-consciousness elements may be obtained separately or together.
The twelve internal [dhātus], excluding form and the rest and that designated as <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: sabhāgaḥ tatsabhāgāśca śeṣāḥ yo na svakarmakṛt // VAkK_1.39 //
children.translated_text: are 'homogeneous' (<s>sabhāga</s>) and 'similar to those' (<s>tatsabhāga</s>); the rest are those which do not perform their own function.

children.text: daśa bhāvanayā heyāḥ pañca ca antyāstrayastridhā /
children.translated_text: Ten are to be abandoned through cultivation; five plus the last three are threefold [to be abandoned];

children.text: na dṛṣṭiheyamakliṣṭaṃ na rūpaṃ nāpyaṣaṣṭhajam // VAkK_1.40 //
children.translated_text: what is not afflicted is not abandoned through [the seeing of] views; nor is form; nor what is born from the sixth [consciousness alone].
Portions of the eye and of the <s>dharmadhātu</s> are 'view' (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>), which is eightfold.
The <s>dhī</s> (discernment) that arises together with the five consciousnesses is not 'view,' because it does not judge.

children.text: cakṣuḥ paśyati rūpāṇi sabhāgaṃ na tadāśritam /
children.translated_text: The eye sees forms — the homogeneous [eye], not the one upon which [the consciousness] depends.

children.text: vijñānaṃ dṛśyate rūpaṃ na kilāntaritaṃ yataḥ // VAkK_1.42 //
children.translated_text: Consciousness [truly] sees form — for it is not [the case that] an obstructed [form] is seen.
One sees with both eyes, because of the clarity of [binocular] seeing.
The eye, ear, and mind [operate on] objects not in contact; the other three otherwise.
By the three — nose and the rest — the apprehension of an equal [i.e., present] object is held.
The support of the last [manovijñāna] is past; the five [sense-consciousnesses] arise simultaneously with their [supports].
Because they undergo modification through its modification, the eye and the rest are the supports [of consciousness].
Because of this exclusiveness, consciousness is designated by them [i.e., 'eye-consciousness,' etc.].

children.text: na kāyasyādharaṃ cakṣuḥ ūrdhvaṃ rūpaṃ na cakṣuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The eye is not below the body, nor is form above the eye;

children.text: vijñānaṃ ca asya rūpaṃ tu kāyasyobhe ca sarvataḥ // VAkK_1.46 //
children.translated_text: and the consciousness of it — but form [is apprehended] on both sides of the body and in all [directions].

children.text: tathā śrotraṃ trayāṇāṃ tu sarvameva svabhūmikam /
children.translated_text: Likewise the ear; for [the objects of] the three [nose, tongue, body], everything belongs to one's own level.
Body-consciousness and the lower level — mind is undetermined [as to level].

children.text: pañca bāhyā divijñeyāḥ nityā dharmā asaṃskṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: The five external [dhātus] are to be known by the gods; the unconditioned <s>dharmas</s> are permanent.

children.text: dharmārdhamindriyaṃ ye ca dvādaśādhyātmikāḥ smṛtāḥ // VAkK_1.48 //
children.translated_text: Half of the <s>dharma</s> [-dhātu] is faculty; and those twelve called 'internal' are remembered [as such].

body.text: abhidharmakośabhāṣye dhātunirdeśo nāma prathamaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptamiti /
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośabhāṣya</s>, the exposition of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) — the first chapter of the Treasury — is concluded.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetusteṣāṃ tathāgato hyavadat /
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: and also their cessation — thus speaks the Great <s>Śramaṇa</s> (Ascetic).

body.translated_text: This was caused to be written by the glorious <s>Lāmāvaka</s>.

children.translated_text: Over four objects, the supremacy of five [faculties]; over two [objects], [the supremacy]
of groups of four and five and eight — in defilement and purification.
Because of supremacy over the obtaining of one's own object, the six faculties [are each a faculty] for all [dharmas].
But due to supremacy over femininity and masculinity, the female and male faculties [derive] from the body.
Because of supremacy over the abiding in a [rebirth] class, defilement,

children.text: jīvitaṃ vedanāḥ pañca śraddhādyāścendriyaṃ matāḥ // VAkK_2.3 //
children.translated_text: and purification — the life [faculty], the five feelings, and faith and the rest are held to be faculties.
The 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty, the 'knowledge' faculty, and the 'one-who-has-known' faculty likewise —
because of supremacy over progressively higher attainment, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and so forth.
The support of mind, its differentiation, its stability, and defilement itself,

children.text: saṃbhāro vyavadānaṃ ca yāvatā tāvadindriyam // VAkK_2.5 //
children.translated_text: the requisites [of the path], and purification — the faculties are as many as these.
From the support, arising, stability, and experience of activity —
fourteen; and likewise the other faculties [derive] from cessation.
The pain-faculty (<s>duḥkhendriya</s>) is the unpleasant bodily feeling; happiness (<s>sukha</s>)

children.text: śātā dhyāne tṛtīye tu caitasī sā sukhendriyam // VAkK_2.7 //
children.translated_text: is the pleasant [bodily feeling]; but in the third <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), that mental [pleasant feeling] is the pleasure-faculty.

children.text: anyatra sā saumanasyaṃ aśātā caitasī punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Elsewhere, that [mental pleasant feeling] is <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure); and the unpleasant mental [feeling]

children.text: daurmanasyamupekṣā tu madhyā ubhayī avikalpanāt // VAkK_2.8 //
children.translated_text: is <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure); <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity) is the middle [feeling], belonging to both [bodily and mental], because it is non-discriminating.
On the paths of seeing, cultivation, and the adept — nine, three, and three are the stainless [faculties];

children.text: rūpīṇi jīvitaṃ duḥkhe sāsravāṇi dvidhā nava // VAkK_2.9 //
children.translated_text: the material ones, the life [faculty], and the pain [faculty] are with-<s>āsravas</s>; nine are twofold.
<s>Vipāka</s> (maturation) is the life [faculty], twofold; twelve, excluding the last eight,

children.text: daurmanasyācca tattvekaṃ savipākaṃ daśa dvidhā // VAkK_2.10 //
children.translated_text: and <s>daurmanasya</s>; that [life-faculty] is one; with maturation, ten are twofold.
Mind, the other feelings, and faith and the rest — the group of eight — are wholesome in two ways;

children.text: daurmanasyaṃ mano 'nyā ca vittistredhā anyadekadhā // VAkK_2.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>daurmanasya</s>, mind, and the other feeling[s] are threefold; the other [faculties are] one way.
Obtained in the desire-realm, excluding the stainless [faculties]; obtained in the form-realm, [excluding] the female and male faculties

children.text: duḥkhe ca hitvā ārūpyāptaṃ sukhe cāpohya rūpi ca // VAkK_2.12 //
children.translated_text: and the pain [faculty]; obtained in the formless realm, [excluding] the pleasure [faculty] and also the material.
The trio of mind and the two feelings are threefold; <s>daurmanasya</s> is to be abandoned in two ways;

children.text: nava bhavanayā pañca tvaheyānyapi na trayam // VAkK_2.13 //
children.translated_text: nine are [abandoned] through cultivation; five are not to be abandoned; and also the three [stainless faculties are not to be abandoned].
In the desire-realm, at first, maturation of two is obtained; not by spontaneously-born beings;

children.text: teḥ ṣaḍ vā sapta vā aṣṭau vā ṣaḍ rūpeṣu ekamuttare // VAkK_2.14 //
children.translated_text: by them, six, or seven, or eight; in the form-realm, six; in the higher [formless realm], one.
In cessation [attainment], having ceased activity, in the formless realm, the life [faculty], mind,

children.text: upekṣāṃ caiva rūpe 'ṣṭau kāme daśa navāṣṭau vā // VAkK_2.15 //
children.translated_text: and equanimity [cease]; in the form realm, eight; in the desire realm, ten, or nine, or eight.

children.text: kramamṛtyau tu catvāri śubhe sarvatra pañca ca /
children.translated_text: At gradual death, four; everywhere, five wholesome [faculties];
the attainment of nine [faculties] at the last two fruits, with seven, eight, or nine [faculties] for the two [pairs].
<s>Arhatva</s> (arhatship) is [attained] with eleven; but it is said that it can occur with one [additional].
One endowed with equanimity, life, and mind necessarily possesses three.
With four [faculties], one possessing the pleasure and body [faculties]; with five, one possessing the eye and the rest;

children.text: saumanasyī ca duḥkhī tu saptabhiḥ strīndriyādimān // VAkK_2.18 //
children.translated_text: and one with <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure); but one with pain possesses seven; one with the female faculty and the rest,
eight; with eleven, one endowed with the 'knowledge' and 'one-who-has-known' faculties.
One endowed with the 'I-shall-come-to-know' faculty possesses thirteen.
One without merit, with the fewest [faculties], possesses eight — excluding [all] but sensation, mind, body [faculties], and life;
an immature person likewise; in the formless realm, [one possesses] equanimity, life, mind, and the wholesome [faculties].
One endowed with the most possesses nineteen, excluding the stainless [faculties];
one of dual sex; a noble one with passion, [possesses] one sex and the two stainless [faculties] excluded.
In the desire realm, an atom without sound has eight substances, without a faculty;
one with the body-faculty has nine substances; one with another faculty has ten substances.
Mind (<s>citta</s>) and mental factors (<s>caittas</s>) necessarily always [arise] together, with all conditioned characteristics;

children.text: prāptyā vā pañcadhā caittā mahābhūmyādibhedataḥ // VAkK_2.23 //
children.translated_text: or [the mental factors are] fivefold, through the division of the great ground (<s>mahābhūmi</s>) and the rest, by means of [their] association.

children.text: vedanā cetanā saṃjñā cchandaḥ sparśo matiḥ smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: Sensation, volition, perception, intention, contact, intelligence, memory,
attention, determination, and concentration in all mental states.
Faith, diligence, tranquility, indifference, modesty, absence of shame,

children.text: mūladvayamahiṃsā ca vīryaṃ ca kuśale sadā // VAkK_2.25 //
children.translated_text: the two roots, non-violence, and energy, always in the skillful.
Delusion, negligence, laziness, lack of faith, sloth, agitation,
in the afflicted, always unskillful, shamelessness, absence of modesty.
Anger, resentment, deceit, envy, stinginess, safeguarding, jealousy,
illusion, pride, and violence, minor afflictive grounds.
Due to initial and sustained thought, in the skillful, in the mind of desire,
twenty-two mental factors, sometimes with remorse as additional.
In the specific, unskillful, with views, also twenty,
with four afflictions, beginning with anger, twenty-one with remorse.
In cessation, eighteen, elsewhere twelve, considered undetermined,

children.text: middhaṃ sarvāvirodhitvādyatra syādadhikaṃ hi tat // VAkK_2.30 //
children.translated_text: where dullness is, without opposition, there it is indeed additional.
Remorse, dullness, unskillful, in the first meditation, therefore are not,
in the subsequent meditation, initial and sustained thought are also beyond.
Lack of shame, heaviness in the blameworthy, fear, and showing of respect,

children.text: prema śraddhā gurutvaṃ hrīḥ te punaḥ kāmarūpayoḥ // VAkK_2.33 //
children.translated_text: affection, faith, respect, these again are the forms of <s>Hrīḥ</s> (modesty) in lustful forms
Movement in speculative thought, generosity, subtlety, pride, elevation,

children.text: madaḥ svadharme raktasya paryādānaṃ tu cetasaḥ // VAkK_2.33 //
children.translated_text: arrogance in one's own duty, attachment, and withdrawal of the mind
Mind, intellect, and consciousness are of one meaning with mental factors,
having support, object forms, and are conjoined in five ways
But the <s>saṃskāras</s> (mental formations) are unassociated, attainment and non-attainment, similarity,

children.text: āsaṃjñikaṃ samāpattī jīvitaṃ lakṣaṇāni ca // VAkK_2.35 //
children.translated_text: non-perception, attainment, life, and characteristics
Names, bodies, etc., thus attainment, gain, and conjunction
Attainment and non-attainment of one's own continuum, and cessation of the fallen ones
Of the three times, threefold, of the auspicious, starting with auspiciousness,
innate, of those who have attained it, and those who have not, fourfold
Threefold for those not to be abandoned, of the learners and non-learners, twofold is considered
Unspecified attainment is innate, except for the <s>Abhijñā</s> (higher knowledge) and <s>Nairmāṇika</s> (illusory body)

children.text: nivṛtasya ca rūpasya kāme rūpasya nāgrajā /
children.translated_text: And of the form of cessation, in desire, of form, not prior-born,
Untroubled, unspecified attainment, of past and future births, threefold
Of those attained from desire, and the pure, the non-attainment of the path is desired
Common personhood is removed by attainment and movement of the base
Similarity of disposition, non-perception among the non-perceivers,
Cessation of mind and mental factors, their fruition is of great result
Thus non-perceptive attainment, in the last meditation, by desire for release
Auspicious, cognizable only by the noble one, one course is obtained
This named cessation, thus, for the purpose of abode, produced by existence,

children.text: śubhā dvivedyāniyatā ca āryasya āpyā prayogataḥ // VAkK_2.43 //
children.translated_text: Auspicious, twofold cognizable, and indeterminate for the noble one, attainable by practice
Attainable enlightenment of the sage, not before the attainment of thirty-four moments
Based on the forms of desire, in beings, named cessation, not among men
Life and lifespan as support, indeed of warmth and consciousness,
Characteristics, rebirth, old age, stability, impermanence
Of their kinds and types, these have the single function of eightfold dharma
The birth of the born is not without cause and conditions
Names, bodies, etc., designations, expressions, syllables,
Known for attained forms of desire, and the outflows are also unspecified

children.text: sabhāgatā sā tu punarvipāko 'pi āptayo dvidhā /
children.translated_text: Similarity, and again fruition, and attainments are twofold

children.text: lakṣaṇāni ca niḥṣyandāḥ samāpattya samanvayāḥ // VAkK_2.48 //
children.translated_text: Characteristics and outflows, attainment, and conjunction
Cause, coexistence, similarity, conjunction,
The all-pervasive, known as fruition, is considered a sixfold cause
From oneself and others, cause, condition, coexistence, mutual results
Like elements, the characteristics of mind and mental factors, as the observed

children.text: caittā dvau saṃvarau teṣāṃ cetaso lakṣaṇāni ca /
children.translated_text: Two mental factors, restraints, and their mental characteristics
Following the mind, with time, results, and auspiciousness, etc.
The similar cause, of one's own kind, the elder
Mutually, the nine grounds, the path, equally distinguished
Born of practice, indeed, of hearing, reflection, and the like
The conjunctional cause is the mind and mental factors, with the same support
Known as the all-pervasive, of the afflicted, in their own ground, previously all-pervasive
The fruition cause, unwholesome and wholesome, indeed with afflictions
The all-pervasive and similar, twofold path, threefold of the three times

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ savisaṃyoga phalaṃ nāsaṃskṛtasya te // VAkK_2.55 //
children.translated_text: Conditioned, with separation, the result, not of the unconditioned
The fruition result of the last, the previous one, the dominant result
The outflow of the similar and all-pervasive, the personal of the two
Fruition, unspecified, the dharma known as disposition, arising from the specified

children.text: niḥṣyando hetusadṛśaḥ visaṃyogaḥ kṣayo dhiyā // VAkK_2.57 //
children.translated_text: The outflow similar to cause, separation, destruction by wisdom
By whose force that is born, that result is produced by effort
Unprecedented, indeed of the conditioned, the conditioned result of the dominant

children.text: varttamānāḥ phalaṃ pañca gṛṇhanti dvau prayacchataḥ /
children.translated_text: The present ones take five results, giving two
The present and past two, one past gives
Afflictions, resultant, and the remaining ones, the first noble ones in sequence

children.text: vipākaṃ sarvagaṃ hitvā tau sabhāgaṃ ca śeṣajāḥ // VAkK_2.60 //
children.translated_text: Abandoning the universal result, those two and the remaining ones are of the same kind
Mind and mental factors, thus also others, devoid of conjunction

children.text: catvāraḥ pratyayā uktāḥ hetvākhyaḥ pañca hetavaḥ // VAkK_2.61 //
children.translated_text: Four causes are stated, called causes, five causes
Mind and mental factors, non-moving, arising immediately after
Object, all phenomena, called cause, is remembered as the chief

children.text: nirudhyamāne kāritraṃ dvau hetū kurutaḥ trayaḥ /
children.translated_text: When being obstructed, two conditions create three

children.text: jāyamāne tato 'nyau tu pratyayau tadviparyayāt // VAkK_2.63 //
children.translated_text: When arising, then the other two conditions, by reversal of that
By four, mind and mental factors indeed, two attainments by three

children.text: dvābhyāmanye tu jāyante neśvarādeḥ kramādibhiḥ // VAkK_2.64 //
children.translated_text: By two, others indeed arise, not by the sequence of <s>Īśvara</s>

children.text: dvidhā bhūtāni taddhetuḥ bhautikasya tu pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: Twice divided, beings, the cause of that, of the material, but fivefold
Thrice the material, mutually, of beings, indeed that is singular
Wholesome and unwholesome in desire, restrained and unrestrained mind
In form and formless, apart from unwholesome, the stainless is twofold

children.text: kāme nava śubhāccittāccittāni aṣṭābhya eva tat /
children.translated_text: In desire, nine from the auspicious mind, indeed from eight, that
From ten, unwholesome, from that four restrained likewise
From five, unrestrained, from that seven minds subsequently

children.text: rūpe daśaikaṃ ca śubhāt navabhyastadanantaram // VAkK_2.68 //
children.translated_text: In form, ten and one from the auspicious, from nine subsequently

children.text: aṣṭābhyo nivṛtaṃ tasmāt ṣaṭ tribhyo 'nivṛtaṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: From eight, restrained, from that six, from three unrestrained again

children.text: tasmāt ṣaṭ evāmārūpye tasya nītiḥ śubhātpunaḥ // VAkK_2.69 //
children.translated_text: From that, six indeed in formless, of that rule, from auspicious again

children.text: nava cittāni tat ṣaṇṇāṃ nivṛtātsapta tattathā /
children.translated_text: Nine minds from that of six, from restrained seven, thus also

children.text: caturbhyaḥ śaikṣam asmāttu pañca aśaikṣaṃ tu pañcakāt // VAkK_2.70 //
children.translated_text: From four, the trainee, from that, five non-trainee, indeed from five
From that, four minds, twelve these, twenty

children.text: prāyogikopapattyāptaṃ śubhaṃ bhittvā triṣu dvidhā // VAkK_2.71 //
children.translated_text: Acquired through practice and rebirth, auspicious, breaking in three, twofold
By resultant, path-bound, skill-based, local and divine
Fourfold, indeterminate in desire, in form devoid of skill

children.text: kliṣṭe traidhātuke lābhaḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ dvayoḥ śubhe /
children.translated_text: In afflicted threefold world, gain of six, six, in two auspicious

children.text: trayāṇāṃ rūpaje śaikṣe caturṇāṃ tasya śeṣite // VAkK_2.73 //
children.translated_text: Of three in form-born, in trainee, four of that remaining

body.text:
abhidharmakośe indriyanirddeśo nāma dvitīyaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptamiti /
śrīlāmāvākasya
body.translated_text:
abhidharmakośe indriyanirddeśo nāma dvitīyaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptamiti /
śrīlāmāvākasya

children.translated_text: Hell-beings, pretas, animals, humans, and six gods
The realm of desire, thus with the division of hell regions, twenty
Above, seventeen places, the realm of form, each separately

children.text: dhyānaṃ tribhūmikaṃ tatra caturthaṃ tvaṣṭabhūmikam // VAkK_3.2 //
children.translated_text: Meditation in three levels, there the fourth in eight levels
The formless realm's place, by rebirth, fourfold

children.text: nikāyaṃ jīvitaṃ cātra niśritā cittasantatiḥ // VAkK_3.3 //
children.translated_text: The group and life here, the continuum of consciousness
The destinations beginning with hell, named as such, five among them
Unafflicted, indeterminate indeed, known as beings, not the intermediate state
Various body perceptions and those with one perception of various bodies
And by reversal, those with one body perception, the formless abode
The consciousness states, seven, the remainder with subdivisions
The beings with the perception of the summit of existence, nine abodes of beings are remembered
Due to the absence of desire, others, four states again

children.text: catvāraḥ sāsravāḥ skandhāḥ svabhūmāveva kevalam // VAkK_3.7 //
children.translated_text: Four with defilements, aggregates in their respective realms only

children.text: vijñānaṃ na sthitiḥ proktaṃ catuṣkoṭi tu saṃgrahe /
children.translated_text: Consciousness is not a state, it is said, fourfold in the summary
Four origins there, of beings, egg-born and others
Fourfold, humans, animals, hell-beings, spontaneously born
Intermediate state gods and also pretas, womb-born
Between death and rebirth, the intermediate existence here
Not having reached the destination, the intermediate existence is not attained
Due to the similarity with the continuity of rice, uninterrupted arising of existence
Due to the unreality of the reflection and dissimilarity, it is not seen
Due to the absence of both together, from the lack of continuity, from the arising of both
Because of the saying of Kaṇṭha, from the Gandharva, from the fivefold statement, according to the path
By the single impulse, he will attain, the previous time's form of existence
He indeed, beyond the moment of rebirth prior to death,
having the vision of pure and divine eyes of the same kind, possessing the force of perfected action,

children.text: sakalākṣaḥ apratighavān anivartyaḥ sa gandhabhuk // VAkK_3.14 //
children.translated_text: having all senses, without obstruction, unreturning, he is a consumer of fragrance.
With a deluded mind, he goes to the destined place with desire,
another, desiring the place of fragrance, having feet upwards, is of hell.
One enters with full awareness; another indeed remains, yet another,
leaves all, another is deluded, eternally born from an egg.
Three enter the womb, of <s>Cakravartin</s> and <s>Swayambhu</s>,
or of both, due to the clarity of action and knowledge, in sequence.
There is no self, only the aggregates, indeed, conditioned by afflictions and actions,
with the continuity of intermediate existence, like a lamp, it enters the womb.
As per the projection, the continuum grows in order, by afflictions and actions,
again goes to the other world, thus the beginningless cycle of existence.
That is dependent origination, with twelve links in three sections,
two at the beginning and end, and eight fully in the middle.
The former afflictions, ten ignorances, are formations of previous actions,
the junction aggregates are consciousness, name, and form thereafter.
Before the arising of the six sense bases, prior to that, from the union of three,
contact, prior to pleasure and pain, from the power of causal knowledge.
Perception, prior to intercourse, thirst for enjoyment, attachment to sexual union,

children.text: upādānaṃ tu bhogānāṃ prāptaye paridhāvataḥ // VAkK_3.23 //
children.translated_text: appropriation indeed, for the attainment of enjoyments, running around.

children.text: sa bhaviṣyat bhavaphalaṃ kurute karma tat bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: He will produce the fruit of becoming through action, that is existence,
Rebirth-linking (<s>pratisaṃdhi</s>) is rebirth (<s>punarjāti</s>); aging-and-death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>) is decay and passing. // VAkK_3.24 //
This [twelvefold chain] pertains to [different] stages and is defiled (<s>kliṣṭa</s>); the enumeration of limbs, however, is based on predominance.
It is for the removal of confusion regarding the former end, the latter end, and the middle. // VAkK_3.25 //

children.text: kleśāstrīṇi dvayaṃ karma sapta vastu phalaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kleśas</s> (defilements) are three [limbs], action (<s>karma</s>) is two, foundation (<s>vastu</s>) is seven, and result (<s>phala</s>) likewise;
the summary of result and cause, and inference about the middle from the two [ends]. // VAkK_3.26 //

children.text: kleśāt kleśaḥ kriyā caiva tato vastu tataḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: From defilement [arises] defilement and action; from that, foundation; from that again,

children.text: vastu kleśāśca jāyante bhavāṅgānāmayaṃ nayaḥ // VAkK_3.27 //
children.translated_text: foundation and defilements arise—this is the principle of the limbs of existence (<s>bhavāṅga</s>). // VAkK_3.27 //
Herein, cause is 'arising' (<s>samutpāda</s>); what has arisen is regarded as the result (<s>phala</s>).
Another <s>dharma</s> that is opposed to knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) [is <s>avidyā</s>], like the words 'enemy' (<s>amitra</s>), 'untruth' (<s>anṛta</s>), and so forth. // VAkK_3.28 //
[Objection:] Since it is called a 'fetter' (<s>saṃyojana</s>) and so on, it is bad wisdom (<s>kuprajñā</s>). [Reply:] No, because of seeing [it differently],
because view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) is said to be associated with it, and because of the teaching that wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is a secondary defilement (<s>upakleśa</s>). // VAkK_3.29 //

children.text: nāma tvarūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ sparśāḥ ṣaṭ saṃnipātajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Name (<s>nāma</s>), however, is the formless <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). The six contacts (<s>sparśa</s>) arise from the conjunction [of three factors];
five are resistance-contact (<s>pratighasaṃsparśa</s>), and the sixth is called designation-contact (<s>adhivacanasaṃsparśa</s>). // VAkK_3.30 //
Contacts are of the types: knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), and the remainder—[corresponding to] stainless, defiled, and the rest.
The contact of ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>) and attraction (<s>anunaya</s>)—the three [feelings] beginning with pleasant feeling (<s>sukhavedanā</s>), etc. // VAkK_3.31 //

children.text: tajjāḥ ṣaḍvedanāḥ pañca kāyikī caitasī parā /
children.translated_text: Born from those are six feelings (<s>vedanā</s>); five are bodily (<s>kāyikī</s>) and the other is mental (<s>caitasī</s>);
and again it is eighteen-fold, from the mental explorations (<s>manopavicāra</s>). // VAkK_3.32 //
In the desire realm (<s>kāma</s>), all [eighteen] have their own objects; in the form realm (<s>rūpin</s>), twelve are the domain;
of the three upper [explorations], in the two [lower] <s>dhyānas</s>, twelve; the desire-realm ones [are found in all four dhyānas]. // VAkK_3.33 //

children.text: svo 'ṣṭālambanam ārūpyo dvayoḥ dhyānadvaye tu ṣaṭ /
children.translated_text: In one's own [realm], eight are the object; in the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>), of the two, in the two <s>dhyānas</s>, six;

children.text: kāmāḥ ṣaṇṇāṃ caturṇā svaḥ ekasyālambanaṃ paraḥ // VAkK_3.34 //
children.translated_text: of the six desire-realm [explorations], four are one's own; one has the other [realm] as its object. // VAkK_3.34 //
Four formless [explorations are in] the two highest [dhyānas]; form-realm ones [number] one [in] the upper [realm];

children.text: eko maule svaviṣayaḥ sarve 'ṣṭādaśa sāsravāḥ // VAkK_3.35 //
children.translated_text: one in the basic [dhyāna has] its own domain; all eighteen are with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>). // VAkK_3.35 //

children.text: uktaṃ ca vakṣyate cānyat atra tu kleśā iṣyate /
children.translated_text: What has been said and what will be said elsewhere—here, however, defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) are intended.
Like a seed, like an elephant, like a root, like a tree, like a husk, likewise, // VAkK_3.36 //
like husk and rice-grain, action is likewise like a medicinal herb and flower;
foundation is like cooked food and drink—in those four [types of] existence (<s>bhava</s>). // VAkK_3.37 //
Birth-existence (<s>upapattibhava</s>) is defiled by all defilements belonging to one's own level (<s>svabhūmika</s>);

children.text: tridhānye traya ārūpye āhārasthitikaṃ jagat // VAkK_3.38 //
children.translated_text: three [types of existence exist] in the other [realms], three in the formless realm. The world subsists on nutriment (<s>āhāra</s>). // VAkK_3.38 //
Morsels of food (<s>kavaḍīkāra āhāra</s>) [exist] in the desire realm, consisting of three sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>);
not the visible-form sense-base (<s>rūpāyatana</s>), because it does not sustain one's own sense-faculties and their objects. // VAkK_3.39 //
Contact (<s>sparśa</s>), volition (<s>cetanā</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) are [the other three] nutriments, with outflows, in the three [realms].
Mind-made (<s>manomaya</s>), seeking existence (<s>saṃbhavaiṣin</s>), the <s>gandharva</s>—[these designate] the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>). // VAkK_3.40 //
And production—here, for the purpose of nourishment, both [refer to] the support and the supported;
the two [others] are for the purpose of impelling to another existence and cessation, respectively, in order. // VAkK_3.41 //
Cutting off, reconnecting, dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), destruction, death (<s>cyuti</s>), and rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>)—
these are held to be [exclusively] in mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>); death and birth [occur] in equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). // VAkK_3.42 //
These two are not in one-pointed [concentration] or non-mind [states]; [death occurs] in the two indeterminate [moral types] (<s>avyākṛta</s>).
Sequential death [occurs] at the feet, navel, and heart; the mind departs [from these]. // VAkK_3.43 //
For those [going to] the lower realms, humans, gods, and elephants, [death occurs] by the cutting of vital points through water and so forth.

Those fixed in the right course (<s>samyaṅniyata</s>) and those fixed in the wrong course (<s>mithyātvaniyata</s>) are <s>Āryas</s> (noble ones) and those who have committed heinous acts (<s>ānantaryakārin</s>). // VAkK_3.44 //
There, regarding the receptacle-world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>), they describe the arrangement below:
a wind-circle (<s>vāyumaṇḍala</s>) of sixteen hundred thousand [yojanas] in height, immeasurable [in breadth]. // VAkK_3.45 //
A water [circle] of eleven hundred and twenty thousand [yojanas] in height;
eight hundred thousand in elevation, the rest becomes gold (<s>kāñcana</s>). // VAkK_3.46 //
Three thousand four hundred and fifty [yojanas] across,
and twelve hundred thousand—[that is] the water-and-gold circle. // VAkK_3.47 //
All around, moreover, threefold. There, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Yugaṃdhara</s>,
<s>Īśādhāra</s>, <s>Khadiraka</s>, mount <s>Sudarśana</s>, likewise, // VAkK_3.48 //
<s>Aśvakarṇa</s>, <s>Vinataka</s>, then mount <s>Nimindhara</s>;

children.text: dvīpāḥ bahiścakravāḍaḥ sapta haimāḥ sa āyasaḥ // VAkK_3.49 //
children.translated_text: the continents (<s>dvīpa</s>) [are] beyond, the <s>Cakravāḍa</s> [mountain is] outermost; seven are golden, that [outermost] one is iron. // VAkK_3.49 //
<s>Meru</s>, made of four gems, [plunges] into the water eighty thousand [yojanas];
above the water, <s>Meru</s> [rises] again eighty thousand [yojanas]. // VAkK_3.50 //
Decreasing by half-and-half for the [next] eight [mountains], and they are equal in height and breadth;
the seven cold [lakes] between them—the first is eighty thousand [yojanas wide]. // VAkK_3.51 //

children.text: ābhyantaraḥ samudro 'sau triguṇaḥ sa tu pārśvataḥ /
children.translated_text: That is the inner ocean; it is threefold [in extent] from the side;

children.text: ardhārdhenāparāḥ śītāḥ śeṣaṃ bāhyo mahodadheḥ // VAkK_3.52 //
children.translated_text: the remaining cold [lakes decrease] by half-and-half; the rest is the outer great ocean. // VAkK_3.52 //

children.text: lakṣatrayaṃ sahasrāṇi viṃśatirdve ca tatra tu /
children.translated_text: Three hundred and twenty-two thousand [yojanas]; and therein,
<s>Jambudvīpa</s> is two thousand [yojanas], with three sides, having the shape of a cart. // VAkK_3.53 //
But one [side] is three and a half <s>yojanas</s>; <s>Pūrvavideha</s> is crescent-shaped;

children.text: pārśvatrayaṃ tathāsya ekaṃ sārdhaṃ triśatayojanam // VAkK_3.54 //
children.translated_text: three of its sides are likewise, and one is three hundred and fifty <s>yojanas</s>. // VAkK_3.54 //
<s>Godānīya</s> is seven and a half thousand [yojanas], circular;

children.text: sārdhe dve madhyamasya aṣṭau caturasraḥ kuruḥ samaḥ // VAkK_3.55 //
children.translated_text: two and a half thousand [yojanas] the middle [diameter]; eight [thousand yojanas for] <s>Uttarakuru</s>, which is square and equal-sided. // VAkK_3.55 //
<s>Deha</s>, <s>Videha</s>, <s>Kurava</s>, <s>Kaurava</s>, <s>Camara</s>, and <s>Avara</s>,
are the eight sub-continents of those; <s>Gāthā</s> and <s>Uttaramantrin</s>. // VAkK_3.56 //
North of here is <s>Kīṭa</s> mountain, nine [yojanas]; beyond that is <s>Himavān</s>,
fifty [yojanas] in breadth and length; a lake [lies] before <s>Gandhamādana</s>. // VAkK_3.57 //
Below, by twenty thousand [yojanas], <s>Avīci</s> [hell] is of that measure;

children.text: tadūrdhvaṃ sapta narakāḥ sarve 'ṣṭau ṣoḍaśotsadāḥ // VAkK_3.58 //
children.translated_text: above it are seven hells (<s>naraka</s>); all eight have sixteen supplementary hells (<s>utsada</s>). // VAkK_3.58 //
A pit of embers (<s>kukūla</s>), a swamp of corpses (<s>kuṇapa</s>), then a razor-path (<s>kṣuramārga</s>) and the like, and a river;
these are in the four directions of those [hells]. The cold [hells] are another eight, beginning with <s>Arbuda</s>. // VAkK_3.59 //
At half [the height] of <s>Meru</s>, the moon and sun [revolve], [each] fifty-one <s>yojanas</s> [in diameter];
midnight is [their] setting; midday is [their] rising, once [per revolution]. // VAkK_3.60 //
In the second month of the rainy season (<s>prāvṛṣ</s>), on the last ninth [day], night begins to increase;

children.text: hemantānāṃ caturthe tu hīyate aharviparyayāt // VAkK_3.61 //
children.translated_text: and in the fourth [month] of winter (<s>hemanta</s>), it decreases; day [increases] in the reverse [manner]. // VAkK_3.61 //
Night and day increase by increments when the sun moves southward and northward [respectively];
observation of the waning moon is due to its own shadow and proximity to the sun. // VAkK_3.62 //
Its four terraces (<s>pariṣaṇḍa</s>) are at intervals of ten thousand [yojanas];

children.text: ṣoḍaśāṣṭau sahasrāṇi catvāri dve ca nirgatāḥ // VAkK_3.63 //
children.translated_text: sixteen, eight, four, and two thousand [yojanas] in extent, projecting outward. // VAkK_3.63 //
In those [terraces dwell] the <s>Karoṭapāṇi</s>, <s>Mālādhāra</s>, <s>Sadāmada</s> [gods],
and the <s>Mahārājika</s> (Great Kings') gods; and also on the seven mountains. // VAkK_3.64 //
On the summit of <s>Meru</s> [dwell] the Thirty-Three (<s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>); that [summit] is eighty thousand [yojanas] in each direction;
at the four corners are peaks inhabited by <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> [guardians]. // VAkK_3.65 //
In the middle, [the city] with two and a half thousand [yojanas] on each side and one and a half <s>yojanas</s> in the middle,

children.text: puraṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma haimaṃ citratalaṃ mṛdu // VAkK_3.66 //
children.translated_text: is the city called <s>Sudarśana</s> (Good to See), golden, with a variegated and soft surface. // VAkK_3.66 //
Therein, the <s>Vaijayanta</s> [palace], with sides of two hundred and fifty [yojanas]; outside, moreover,
that [city] is adorned with [the parks] <s>Caitraratha</s>, <s>Pāruṣya</s>, <s>Miśra</s>, and <s>Nandana</s>. // VAkK_3.67 //
Twenty [yojanas] apart, these [parks have] beautiful grounds in the four directions;
to the northeast [stands] the <s>Pārijāta</s> [tree], to the southwest the <s>Sudharmā</s> [assembly hall]. // VAkK_3.68 //

children.text: tata ūrdhva vimāneṣu devāḥ kāmabhujastu ṣaṭ /
children.translated_text: Above that, in celestial palaces (<s>vimāna</s>), [dwell] the gods; those enjoying desire (<s>kāma</s>) are six [classes];
[their] sexual union [is respectively through] pairing, embrace, hand-holding, mutual holding, glancing, and looking. // VAkK_3.69 //
A child [the equivalent of] five years up to [the equivalent of] ten years [in age]
is born among these [gods]; they are fully formed and clothed, and are material beings (<s>rūpin</s>). // VAkK_3.70 //
Three [are] desire-mode births (<s>kāmopapatti</s>); the desire-gods together with humans;
three [are] pleasure-mode births (<s>sukhopapatti</s>)—the nine levels of the three <s>dhyānas</s>. // VAkK_3.71 //
From [any] station, downward [one can see] as far as that; upward [one can see] the same distance from each successive [station];
there is no upward seeing for these [beings], except through supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>) or another's influence. // VAkK_3.72 //
The four continents, moon and sun, <s>Meru</s>, the desire-realm heaven-dwellers,
and the <s>Brahma</s>-world — a thousand of these constitute a small chiliocosm (<s>sāhasra cūḍika</s>). // VAkK_3.73 //
A thousand of those is the middle world-system (<s>dvisāhasra lokadhātu</s>);
a thousand of those is the great trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasra</s>), [which undergoes] equal evolution and dissolution. // VAkK_3.74 //
The beings of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> are in measure three and a half cubits (<s>hasta</s>);
with a double increase in succession, those of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, <s>Godānīya</s>, and <s>Uttarakuru</s>. // VAkK_3.75 //
With increase by a quarter [cubit], slender, up to one and a half <s>krośa</s> for the heaven-dwellers;

children.text: kāmināṃ rūpiṇāṃ tvādau yojanārdhaṃ tataḥ param // VAkK_3.76 //
children.translated_text: for the desire-[realm gods], the form-[realm gods] at first [are] half a <s>yojana</s>, then increasingly. // VAkK_3.76 //
With half-and-half increase upward, beginning from the <s>Parīttābha</s> [gods], the body;
doubling and doubling, except for the <s>Anabhraka</s> [gods], three <s>yojanas</s>. // VAkK_3.77 //
In <s>Uttarakuru</s>, the lifespan is a thousand [years]; for the other two, less by half-and-half;

children.text: ihāniyatam ante tu daśābdāḥ ādito 'mitam // VAkK_3.78 //
children.translated_text: here [in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>] it is indefinite; at the end [of a cosmic cycle], ten years; at the beginning, immeasurable. // VAkK_3.78 //
Fifty human years equal one day-and-night for the lowest heaven-dwellers
in the desire [realm]; by that [reckoning], their lifespan is five hundred years. // VAkK_3.79 //
For each successively higher [class], both [the day-length and lifespan] double; for the form-realm gods, however,
there is no day-and-night, and lifespan is [measured] in <s>kalpas</s> equal to their [respective] abodes. // VAkK_3.80 //
In the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>), twenty thousand <s>kalpas</s>, each [higher level] increasingly more;
a great <s>kalpa</s> [is reckoned] from the <s>Parīttābha</s> [level]; below that, [they are reckoned in terms of] lower [kalpas]. // VAkK_3.81 //
The lifespans of desire-realm gods equal [in days] one day-and-night respectively, in order,
in [the hells] <s>Saṃjīva</s> and the [next] five; by those [reckonings], their lifespan is like that of the desire-gods. // VAkK_3.82 //
Half [a kalpa in] <s>Pratāpana</s>; in <s>Avīci</s>, an intermediate <s>kalpa</s> (<s>antaraḥkalpa</s>); the last, moreover,

children.text: kalpaṃ tiraścāṃ pretānāṃ māsānhā śatapañcakam // VAkK_3.83 //
children.translated_text: a [full] <s>kalpa</s>. For animals (<s>tiryañc</s>) and hungry ghosts (<s>preta</s>), the maximum [lifespan] is five hundred months. // VAkK_3.83 //
By removing one sesame seed per century from a granary, the lifespan [of <s>Arbuda</s> hell is its] exhaustion;
the other [cold hells, beginning with] <s>Arbuda</s>, have lifespans increasing by a multiple of twenty. // VAkK_3.84 //
Outside <s>Uttarakuru</s>, there is untimely death. Atoms (<s>paramāṇu</s>), syllables (<s>akṣara</s>), and moments (<s>kṣaṇa</s>)
are the ultimate limits of matter (<s>rūpa</s>), name (<s>nāma</s>), and time (<s>adhvan</s>); [the smallest are] atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) and fine particle (<s>aṇu</s>), likewise. // VAkK_3.85 //
Iron, water, rabbit[-hair], ram[-wool], cow[-hair], mote-in-sunbeam, louse-egg, louse — arising from those,
barley-grain, and finger-joint — each should be known as seven times [the preceding]. // VAkK_3.86 //
Twenty-four finger-widths make a cubit (<s>hasta</s>); four cubits make a bow-length (<s>dhanus</s>);

children.text: dhanuḥ pañcaśatānyeṣāṃ krośo raṇyaṃ ca tanmatam // VAkK_3.87 //
children.translated_text: five hundred of these make a <s>krośa</s>, and that is also considered a <s>raṇya</s> (league). // VAkK_3.87 //
Eight of those make a <s>yojana</s>, they say. Twenty [times] a hundred [instants] again

children.text: tatkṣaṇaḥ te punaḥ ṣaṣṭirlavaḥ triṃśad guṇottarāḥ // VAkK_3.88 //
children.translated_text: make one moment (<s>tatkṣaṇa</s>); sixty of those make a <s>lava</s>; thirty increasing in succession, // VAkK_3.88 //
three <s>muhūrtas</s> [make] a day-and-night; twelve months [make a year];

children.text: saṃvatsaraḥ sonarātraḥ kalpo bahuvidhaḥ smṛtaḥ // VAkK_3.89 //
children.translated_text: a year, with its days and nights — <s>kalpas</s> are declared to be of many kinds. // VAkK_3.89 //
The dissolution-<s>kalpa</s> (<s>saṃvarttakalpa</s>) [extends] from the arising of [beings in] the hells to the destruction of the receptacle-[world];
the evolution-<s>kalpa</s> (<s>vivartakalpa</s>) [extends] from the prior wind to the arising of [beings in] the hells. // VAkK_3.90 //
An intermediate <s>kalpa</s> (<s>antaraḥkalpa</s>) [extends] from immeasurable [lifespan] down to a ten-year lifespan; from that,

children.text: utkarṣā apakarṣāśca kalpā aṣṭā daśāpare // VAkK_3.91 //
children.translated_text: the increases and decreases — the other <s>kalpas</s> are eighteen. // VAkK_3.91 //
One increase [goes] from those up to eighty thousand years of lifespan;

children.text: iti loko vivṛtto 'yaṃ kalpāṃstiṣṭhati viṃśatim // VAkK_3.92 //
children.translated_text: thus this world, having evolved, abides for twenty <s>kalpas</s>. // VAkK_3.92 //
Then it dissolves; having dissolved, it remains [dissolved]; it evolves [again] equally;
these [four phases of twenty kalpas each] make eighty — [that is] a great <s>kalpa</s> (<s>mahākalpa</s>); from three incalculable [aeons] (<s>asaṃkhya</s>) of those arises // VAkK_3.93 //
<s>Buddhahood</s> (<s>buddhatva</s>). In the decreasing [phase], from a hundred[-year lifespan] down to that [ten-year lifespan] a [Buddha] arises;
for the two [types], <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> — the rhinoceros-like (<s>khaḍga</s>) [type] follows a hundred <s>kalpas</s>. // VAkK_3.94 //
A <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) does not arise [when lifespan is] below eighty thousand years;
gold, silver, copper, and iron wheel-turners — they [rule over continents] in descending order. // VAkK_3.95 //

children.text: ekadvitricaturdvīpāḥ na ca dvau saha buddhavat /
children.translated_text: [They rule] one, two, three, and four continents [respectively]; two do not [arise] simultaneously, like <s>Buddhas</s>;
[the four wheel-turners are distinguished by enemies'] going forth [voluntarily], coming on their own, being subdued by weapons, or being killed by weapons. // VAkK_3.96 //
By partial, standing, heated, and full [marks], the distinguishing marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) of the Sage (<s>muni</s>) are superior.

children.text: prāgāsan rūpivat sattvāḥ rasarāgāttataḥ śanaiḥ // VAkK_3.97 //
children.translated_text: Formerly, beings were like form-realm [gods]; then, from attachment to taste (<s>rasarāga</s>), gradually, // VAkK_3.97 //
from laziness, they made stores; a field-protector (<s>kṣetrapa</s>) was hired by those with possessions;
then, from the increase of paths of <s>karma</s> (action), when [lifespan] diminished to ten years, // VAkK_3.98 //
the <s>kalpa</s> ends through weapons, disease, and famine;

children.text: divasān sapta māsāṃśca varṣāṇi ca yathākramam // VAkK_3.99 //
children.translated_text: [lasting] seven days, seven months, and seven years, respectively, in order. // VAkK_3.99 //
The destructions [of the world] are again three — by fire, water, and wind.

children.text: dhyānatrayaṃ dvitīyādi śīrṣa tāsāṃ yathākramam // VAkK_3.100 //
children.translated_text: The second, third, and [fourth] <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) are respectively the upper limits of those [destructions]. // VAkK_3.100 //
Because of the similarity with what [they] wash away, [destruction does] not [occur] in the fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>] — because of its imperturbability (<s>aniñjana</s>).

children.text: na nityaṃ saha sattvena tadvimānodayavyayāt // VAkK_3.101 //
children.translated_text: [The world-vessel] is not permanent together with the beings, because of the arising and perishing of their celestial mansions (<s>vimāna</s>). // VAkK_3.101 //

children.text: saptāgninā adbhirekā evaṃ gate 'dbhiḥ saptake punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seven [destructions] by fire, one by water; when such a [cycle of seven-plus-one] has passed, again seven [cycles] by water,
then a sevenfold [cycle] by fire; after that, the wind-destruction. // VAkK_3.102 //

body.text: abhidharmakośabhāṣye lokanirdeśo nāma tṛtīyaṃ kośasthānam samāptamiti /
body.translated_text: Thus is completed the third chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa-bhāṣya</s>, entitled 'Exposition of the World' (<s>Lokanirdeśa</s>).
May the merit herein be for the glorious <s>Lāmāvāka</s>.

children.text: karmajaṃ lokavaicitryaṃ cetanā tatkṛtaṃ ca tat /
children.translated_text: The diversity of the world is born from <s>karma</s> (action); <s>cetanā</s> (volition) and what is produced by it — that is [<s>karma</s>].

children.text: cetanā mānasaṃ karma tajjaṃ vākkāyakarmaṇī // VAkK_4.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cetanā</s> is mental <s>karma</s>; what is born from it is verbal and bodily <s>karma</s>. // VAkK_4.1 //
Those [latter] two are <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action) and <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action). Bodily <s>vijñapti</s> is held to be

children.text: saṃsthānaṃ na gatiryasmātsaṃskṛtaṃ kṣaṇikaṃ vyayāt // VAkK_4.2 //
children.translated_text: a configuration (<s>saṃsthāna</s>), not a movement (<s>gati</s>) — because what is conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) is momentary, due to destruction. // VAkK_4.2 //

children.text: na kasyacidahetoḥ syāt hetuḥ syācca vināśakaḥ /
children.translated_text: No [entity] can be without a cause, and a cause would be a destroyer [of the entity].

children.text: dvigrāhyaṃ syāt na cāṇau tat vāgvijñaptistu vāgdhvaniḥ // VAkK_4.3 //
children.translated_text: It would be apprehended by two [senses]; and an atom does not have that [configuration]. Verbal <s>vijñapti</s> is speech-sound. // VAkK_4.3 //
The three [kinds — wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate] are [established] through assertions [such as] 'stainless form,' 'increase,' 'non-performance,' 'path,' and so forth.
After the [first] moment, <s>avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action) is obtained in the desire realm (<s>kāma</s>), [and arises] from past and present [great] elements. // VAkK_4.4 //
Bodily and verbal <s>karma</s> with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) depends on its own [set of] great elements;
the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) [<s>karma</s> depends on elements] where [the being] is born; <s>avijñapti</s> is unappropriated (<s>anupāttika</s>). // VAkK_4.5 //
The outflow-born (<s>naiḥṣyandikī</s>) [<s>avijñapti</s>] is called 'belonging to a sentient being' — born from great elements that are outflow-derived and appropriated.
That born from <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is 'accreted' (<s>pacayikā</s>) — born from unappropriated and undifferentiated great elements. // VAkK_4.6 //
There is no indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>) <s>avijñapti</s>. It is threefold [wholesome, unwholesome, and that which is neither]. The unwholesome again

[exists] in the desire realm; <s>avijñapti</s> [exists] also in the form realm; <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action) [exists only] in those [two realms] with <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought). // VAkK_4.7 //
In the desire realm too, there is no <s>nivṛta</s> (obscured [but indeterminate avijñapti]) — because there is no origination from the immediately past [mind].
In the ultimate sense, the wholesome is liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>); [arising] from itself, the roots [are] <s>hrī</s> (shame) and <s>apatrāpā</s> (embarrassment). // VAkK_4.8 //
By association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>), [other dharmas] conjoined with those [are wholesome]; by origination (<s>samutthāna</s>), action and so forth.
The unwholesome is the reverse; the ultimately indeterminate is the two stable [categories]. // VAkK_4.9 //
Origination (<s>samutthāna</s>) is twofold: that which is called 'causal' (<s>hetu</s>) and 'that-moment-arising.'
Of those two, the first is the instigator (<s>pravartaka</s>); the second is the continuer (<s>anuvartaka</s>). // VAkK_4.10 //
The instigating [consciousness], to be abandoned by seeing (<s>dṛṣṭi-heya</s>), is mental (<s>vijñāna</s>); but both [types exist].
The mental [consciousness] to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanā-heya</s>) — [and the] fivefold [sense-consciousnesses] are continuers. // VAkK_4.11 //
Even when the instigator is wholesome and so forth, the continuer may be threefold.

children.text: tulyaṃ muneḥ śubhaṃ yāvat nobhayaṃ tu vipākajam // VAkK_4.12 //
children.translated_text: Of the Sage, [the continuer is] equal to the wholesome [instigator] throughout; but retribution-born [<s>karma</s>] is not both. // VAkK_4.12 //
<s>Avijñapti</s> (non-manifest action) should be known as threefold: restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>), non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>), and the other [i.e., intermediate].
Restraint is [named] <s>prātimokṣa</s> (individual liberation), born of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and likewise undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>). // VAkK_4.13 //
The <s>prātimokṣa</s>-[restraint] is eightfold; but in substance it is fourfold.

children.text: liṅgato nāmasaṃcārāt pṛthak te cāvirodhinaḥ // VAkK_4.14 //
children.translated_text: [They are divided] by gender (<s>liṅga</s>), by the circulation of name, [and by being] separate and non-contradictory. // VAkK_4.14 //
Through taking the vow of abstinence from five, eight, ten, and all [transgressions] to be avoided—
[one becomes] a lay devotee (<s>upāsaka</s>), a fasting-vow holder (<s>upavāsa-stha</s>), a novice (<s>śramaṇa-uddeśa</s>), and a fully ordained monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>). // VAkK_4.15 //
Morality (<s>śīla</s>) is good conduct (<s>sucarita</s>) and <s>karma</s>; and it is also called restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>).
In the first [i.e., <s>prātimokṣa</s>], there are both <s>vijñapti</s> and <s>avijñapti</s>; the <s>prātimokṣa</s> action-path. // VAkK_4.16 //
The eight [types of persons] endowed with <s>prātimokṣa</s> [restraint]; one endowed with that born of <s>dhyāna</s>;
with the undefiled [restraint], the noble beings (<s>ārya-sattvas</s>); the last two [restraints] follow the mind. // VAkK_4.17 //
[Restraints arising] in <s>ānāgamya</s> (access concentration) are called 'of abandonment' — those two arise from the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantarya-mārga</s>).
[The other] two [called] 'clear comprehension' (<s>saṃprajñāna</s>) and 'mindfulness' (<s>smṛti</s>) are the restraints of mind-faculty. // VAkK_4.18 //
One established in <s>prātimokṣa</s> is always, until its abandonment, endowed with present
<s>avijñapti</s>; from the moment after the first [instant], [he is endowed] with past [<s>avijñapti</s>]. // VAkK_4.19 //
Likewise one established in non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>); one possessing <s>dhyāna</s>-restraint is always [endowed with it].
But the noble one (<s>ārya</s>) — not with past [<s>avijñapti</s>] in the first [moment]; [endowed] with the unborn [future <s>avijñapti</s>]. // VAkK_4.20 //
The concentrated one and the one on the noble path — those two are endowed with the present [<s>avijñapti</s>].

children.text: madhyasthasyāsti cedādau madhyayā ūrdhvaṃ dvikālayā // VAkK_4.21 //
children.translated_text: If the intermediate one [<s>avijñapti</s>] exists at first, [then one is endowed] with the middle one; afterward, with [<s>avijñapti</s> of] two times. // VAkK_4.21 //
One established in non-restraint [is endowed] with unwholesome [<s>avijñapti</s>]; one established in restraint, with wholesome [<s>avijñapti</s>].
One is endowed with <s>avijñapti</s> as long as the force of faith or defilement [continues]. // VAkK_4.22 //

children.text: vijñaptyā tu punaḥ sarve kurvanto madhyayānvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: But with <s>vijñapti</s> (manifest action), all those who are performing [it] are endowed with the present [<s>vijñapti</s>].
From the moment after [the action], with the past [<s>vijñapti</s>], until its abandonment; there is none with the unborn [<s>vijñapti</s>]. // VAkK_4.23 //
One is not endowed with both an obscured (<s>nivṛta</s>) and an unobscured [<s>avijñapti</s>] that are past.

children.text: asaṃvaro duścaritaṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ karma tatpathaḥ // VAkK_4.24 //
children.translated_text: Non-restraint (<s>asaṃvara</s>) is misconduct (<s>duścarita</s>), bad morality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>), <s>karma</s>, and its path. // VAkK_4.24 //
The intermediate one is endowed with <s>vijñapti</s> alone while performing [it]; [he is] of mild volition.
[One whose] <s>vijñapti</s> is abandoned or unborn — [yet having] <s>avijñapti</s> — is a noble person (<s>ārya-pudgala</s>). // VAkK_4.25 //
That born of <s>dhyāna</s> is obtained only in the <s>dhyāna</s>-plane; the undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) likewise in that [plane].
The noble one [obtains] <s>prātimokṣa</s> through being informed by another and so forth. // VAkK_4.26 //
The undertaking [of <s>prātimokṣa</s> is] for life; for a day and night from the conventional [<s>saṃvṛti</s>, i.e., the fasting vow].
Non-restraint does not [last merely] a day and night — because it is not so taken up. // VAkK_4.27 //
The fasting-vow (<s>upavāsa</s>) should be taken in the early morning, from another [person], [while] bowing low, [by one] standing, [through] the recitation of what is stated.
The fasting-vow [requires] complete limbs, [is for one] without adornments, [and] does not expire at nightfall. // VAkK_4.28 //
The limbs of morality (<s>śīla</s>), the limb of non-negligence (<s>apramāda</s>), and the limbs of the vow (<s>vrata</s>) — in order —

children.text: catvāryekaṃ tathā trīṇi smṛtināśo madaśca taiḥ // VAkK_4.29 //
children.translated_text: are four, one, and three. By those [lapses in them come] loss of mindfulness and intoxication. // VAkK_4.29 //
The fasting-vow exists for others also [i.e., non-Buddhists]; but there is no refuge (<s>śaraṇa</s>) for one who has not gone [to the Three Refuges].
The becoming of a lay-devotee (<s>upāsaka</s>) [comes] from taking refuge — but the utterance from convention, like [the ordination of] a <s>bhikṣu</s>. // VAkK_4.30 //
If all [precepts] are restrained [at once], how [can there be] partial observances and so forth?

children.text: tatpalanāt kila proktāḥ mṛdvāditvaṃ yathā manaḥ // VAkK_4.31 //
children.translated_text: They are said [to be partial] because of that guarding — just as mildness etc. [of mind designate] different types. // VAkK_4.31 //
He who takes the threefold refuge goes to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the <s>dharmas</s> that constitute [them], the adepts (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), those of both [stages],

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ ceti śaraṇaṃ yo yāti śaraṇatrayam // VAkK_4.32 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Nirvāṇa</s> — that is refuge. // VAkK_4.32 //
Because sexual misconduct (<s>mithyācāra</s>) is extremely blameworthy, because of ease [of observance], because of attaining [merely] non-performance—

children.text: yathābhyupagamaṃ lābhaḥ saṃvarasya na saṃtate // VAkK_4.33 //
children.translated_text: [restraint] is obtained according to one's undertaking, not in the [mental] continuum. // VAkK_4.33 //
And because of the unwanted consequence of false speech [if one claimed total restraint], in the violation of all trainings—
from the rejection of [one specific] fault, [merely] for the purpose of non-guarding — liquor alone. // VAkK_4.34 //
From all and from both [kinds of beings], obtained in the desire realm, from those [who are] presently [existing]—
[is obtained the prātimokṣa]; from the fundamental [dharmas], at all times — the <s>dhyāna</s> and undefiled restraints. // VAkK_4.35 //
Restraint [operates] toward all beings; there is debate [regarding certain] limbs and causes.

children.text: asaṃvarastu sarvebhyaḥ sarvāṅgebhyo na kāraṇaiḥ // VAkK_4.36 //
children.translated_text: Non-restraint too [is] toward all [beings], from all limbs — not [merely] from causes. // VAkK_4.36 //
Non-restraint is obtained through performance or through [explicit] undertaking.
The remaining <s>avijñapti</s> is obtained through the field (<s>kṣetra</s>), the gift, respect, and exertion. // VAkK_4.37 //
The abandonment of <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint [occurs] through renunciation of training (<s>śikṣā-nikṣepaṇa</s>), death,
the arising of both sex-characteristics, cutting the [wholesome] roots, and the passing of the night. // VAkK_4.38 //
And through a <s>pātanīya</s> (defeat-entailing offence) — so say some; [through the] disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s> — [say] others.
But the <s>Kāśmīras</s> accept both [loss of restraint and the debt-like obligation] for one who has committed [a <s>pātanīya</s>], like a debt. // VAkK_4.39 //
The wholesome [restraint] obtained in <s>dhyāna</s> is abandoned through moving to [another] plane and through loss [of the <s>dhyāna</s>].
Likewise that obtained in the formless [realm]; but the noble one's [restraint is lost] through attainment of the fruit, being 'heated,' and loss [of faculties]. // VAkK_4.40 //
Non-restraint [is lost] through attainment of restraint, death, and the arising of both sex-characteristics.
The intermediate [<s>avijñapti</s> is lost] through [loss of] force, gift-giving, [change of] purpose, [end of] lifespan, and cutting the roots. // VAkK_4.41 //
Unwholesome [<s>avijñapti</s>] obtained in the desire realm that is formless — [is lost] through cutting the roots and birth in a higher [realm].
The afflicted [<s>avijñapti</s>] is destroyed through the arising of the antidote; formless [<s>avijñapti</s>] is destroyed through loss. // VAkK_4.42 //
Non-restraint [exists] for humans, excluding <s>śaṇḍha</s> (eunuch), <s>paṇḍaka</s> (sexually deficient), those of dual form, [and]

children.text: kurūṃśca saṃvaro 'pyevaṃ devānāṃ ca nṛṇāṃ trayaḥ // VAkK_4.43 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Kurus</s>. Restraint [exists] likewise. For gods and humans, three [kinds exist]. // VAkK_4.43 //
For gods born in the desire and form [realms], there is <s>dhyāna</s>-born [restraint]; and the undefiled [restraint exists]
also for formless beings, excluding those in the <s>dhyānāntara</s> (intermediate meditation) and the non-percipient beings (<s>asaṃjñi-sattva</s>). // VAkK_4.44 //
<s>Karma</s> that is safe (<s>kṣema</s>), unsafe (<s>akṣema</s>), and other — [that is,] wholesome, unwholesome, and other;

children.text: puṇyāpuṇyamaniñjaṃ ca sukhevedyādi ca trayam // VAkK_4.45 //
children.translated_text: meritorious (<s>puṇya</s>), demeritorious (<s>apuṇya</s>), and imperturbable (<s>aniñja</s>) — and the triad of that which is experienced as pleasure, etc. // VAkK_4.45 //
In the desire realm, wholesome <s>karma</s> is meritorious; imperturbable [<s>karma</s>] belongs to the upper [realms].

children.text: tadbhūmiṣu yataḥ karmavipākaṃ prati neñjati // VAkK_4.46 //
children.translated_text: Because in those planes, <s>karma</s> does not waver (<s>na iñjati</s>) with respect to [its] retribution (<s>vipāka</s>). // VAkK_4.46 //
Wholesome [<s>karma</s>] is experienced as pleasure [from the first] <s>dhyāna</s> up to the third; beyond that,
it is experienced as neither-suffering-nor-pleasure; but the unwholesome is experienced as suffering here [in the desire realm]. // VAkK_4.47 //
Below [in the desire realm] too, some [hold that] intermediate [<s>karma</s>] exists — because of retribution in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>.
Because the first and last retributions of the three are accepted [as simultaneous]. // VAkK_4.48 //
By own-nature, by association (<s>saṃprayoga</s>), by object (<s>ālambana</s>), by retribution (<s>vipāka</s>),
and by direct confrontation (<s>sa���mukhībhāva</s>) — thus the 'to-be-experienced' character is fivefold. // VAkK_4.49 //
And that [<s>karma</s>] is determinate and indeterminate; the determinate is again threefold—
from being experienced in this life and so forth; some [hold that <s>karma</s> is] fivefold. // VAkK_4.50 //
Others [say] there is a fourfold set of propositions (<s>catuṣkoṭi</s>); the projection of a birth-state (<s>nikāya</s>) is by three.

children.text: sarvatra caturākṣepaḥ śubhasya narake tridhā // VAkK_4.51 //
children.translated_text: And the four-[types-of-<s>karma</s>] project everywhere; wholesome [<s>karma</s> projects] into hell in three ways. // VAkK_4.51 //
A foolish person (<s>bāla</s>) who is dispassionate and stable [regarding a realm] does not perform <s>karma</s> to be experienced at birth there;
nor does a noble one perform <s>karma</s> to be experienced elsewhere; nor [does one who is] unstable in the desire realm or in the highest [realm]. // VAkK_4.52 //
[<s>Karma</s> is] twenty-two-fold in the desire realm — the intermediate existence (<s>antarā-bhava</s>) projects [it].

children.text: dṛṣṭadharmaphalaṃ tacca nikāyo hyeka eva saḥ // VAkK_4.53 //
children.translated_text: And that is <s>karma</s> whose fruit is visible [in this life] — for that [intermediate existence] is indeed a single birth-state (<s>nikāya</s>). // VAkK_4.53 //
What is done with intense defilement or faith, continuously,

children.text: guṇakṣetre ca niyataṃ tatpitrorghātakaṃ ca yat // VAkK_4.54 //
children.translated_text: and in a meritorious field (<s>guṇa-kṣetra</s>) — that is determinate; and that which kills one's parents. // VAkK_4.54 //
<s>Karma</s> whose fruit is visible [in this life arises] from the special features of the field and intention.

children.text: tadbhūmyatyantavairāgyāt vipāke niyataṃ hi yat // VAkK_4.55 //
children.translated_text: Because of complete dispassion for that plane — whatever is determinate with respect to retribution, // VAkK_4.55 //

those who have arisen from the <s>nirodha</s> (cessation attainment), the <s>ara���ā</s> (non-conflict meditation), <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), the [path of] seeing, or the fruit of <s>arhatship</s>—
a benefit or harm done to them, its fruit is experienced immediately. // VAkK_4.56 //
The feeling that is the retribution of wholesome <s>karma</s> that is non-deliberative (<s>avitarka</s>)
is held to be purely mental (<s>caitasikī</s>); but bodily (<s>kāyikī</s>) [feeling is the retribution] of the unwholesome. // VAkK_4.57 //
Mental distraction is [derangement] of the mind in [the realm of] mind-and-consciousness; and that is born from the retribution of <s>karma</s>—
through fear, injury, imbalance, and grief — and for those in the desire realm [who are] not in the <s>Kurus</s>. // VAkK_4.58 //
The statement of 'crooked,' 'faulty,' and 'impure' — [these refer to <s>karma</s>] born of hypocrisy (<s>śāṭhya</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and passion (<s>rāga</s>) [respectively].
Again, <s>karma</s> is fourfold by the division of black, white, and so forth. // VAkK_4.59 //
Unwholesome [<s>karma</s>], obtained in the form and desire [realms], and wholesome — in order —
[these constitute] black, white, and both; for the destruction of those, [there is] the outflow-free (<s>nirāsrava</s>) [<s>karma</s>]. // VAkK_4.60 //
In the [eight] <s>dharma-kṣāntis</s> (dharma-acceptances), in dispassion, and in the eight uninterrupted paths—

children.text: yā cetanā dvādaśadhā karma kṛṣṇakṣayāya tat // VAkK_4.61 //
children.translated_text: the volitions therein, twelvefold — that <s>karma</s> is for the destruction of the black. // VAkK_4.61 //

children.text: navame cetanā yā sā kṛṣṇaśuklakṣayāya ca /
children.translated_text: The volition in the ninth [uninterrupted path] — that is for the destruction of both black and white.
For [the destruction of] the white — that born from the final uninterrupted path in the <s>dhyāna</s>-dispassions. // VAkK_4.62 //
Others know [the first type as] 'to be experienced in hell' — and the second as 'to be experienced in the desire realm' in both [ways].

children.text: dṛgdheyaṃ kṛṣṇamanye anyatkṛṣṇaśuklaṃ tu kāmajam // VAkK_4.63 //
children.translated_text: Others [say] that to be abandoned by seeing is 'black'; the other, 'black-and-white' — but [only what is] born in the desire realm. // VAkK_4.63 //
The <s>karma</s> of body, speech, and mind of an adept (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) — in order —

children.text: maunatrayam tridhā śaucaṃ sarva sucaritatrayam // VAkK_4.64 //
children.translated_text: [constitutes] the threefold silence (<s>mauna</s>); the threefold purity (<s>śauca</s>); all [three] are the triad of good conduct. // VAkK_4.64 //
Unwholesome bodily <s>karma</s> and the like is considered the triad of misconduct.
Even what is not [technically] <s>karma</s> — <s>abhidhyā</s> (covetousness) and the like — is the threefold mental misconduct. // VAkK_4.65 //
Good conduct is the reverse [of misconduct]; because of their inclusion as the coarse [manifestations] of those,

children.text: daśa karmapathā uktā yathāyogaṃ śubhāśubhāḥ // VAkK_4.66 //
children.translated_text: ten action-paths (<s>karma-pathas</s>) are stated — wholesome and unwholesome as appropriate. // VAkK_4.66 //
Six unwholesome [paths are] <s>avijñapti</s>; one is twofold [<s>vijñapti</s> and <s>avijñapti</s>]; those [paths] of one who performs [them]

children.text: dvividhāḥ sapta kuśalāḥ avijñaptiḥ samādhijāḥ // VAkK_4.67 //
children.translated_text: are twofold; the seven wholesome [paths are] <s>avijñapti</s> born of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). // VAkK_4.67 //
But [in the] preparatory [stages] (<s>sāmantaka</s>), [there is] <s>vijñapti</s>; <s>avijñapti</s> may or may not exist.
In the subsequent stages (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>), the reverse; the preparatory [action] is born from three roots. // VAkK_4.68 //
[<s>Abhidhyā</s>] and the like, arising immediately after [the action-path], are born from three roots.
The wholesome [paths], together with [their] preparatory [stages] and conclusions, are born from non-attachment, non-hatred, and non-delusion. // VAkK_4.69 //
Killing, malice, and harsh speech are completed through hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>); through greed (<s>lobha</s>) —
going to another's wife, covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>), and taking what is not given are completed. // VAkK_4.70 //
But wrong view (<s>mithyā-dṛṣṭi</s>) [is completed] through delusion (<s>moha</s>); of the rest, [completion] is accepted [as being] from all three [roots].

children.text: sattvabhogāvadhiṣṭhānaṃ nāmarūpaṃ ca nāma ca // VAkK_4.71 //
children.translated_text: Beings, possessions — [are] the basis; name-and-form, and name [alone — are the basis for the last two]. // VAkK_4.71 //

children.text: samaṃ prāk ca mṛtasyāsti na maulaḥ anyāśrayodayāt /
children.translated_text: Equally, [the basis] exists before and for one who has died; the fundamental [action-path does] not — because of the arising of another basis.
In armies and such, because of a single common purpose, all are connected as agents. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.72 //
<s>Prāṇātipāta</s> (taking life) is the intentional killing of another without confusion;
<s>adattādāna</s> (taking what is not given) is appropriating another's property by force or theft. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.73 //
Going to one who should not be approached—<s>kāmamithyācāra</s> (sexual misconduct) is fourfold;
a statement to one who understands the meaning, by one who has a contrary cognition, is <s>mṛṣāvacas</s> (false speech). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.74 //
What is experienced by the eye, ear, mind, and consciousness, and by the three [remaining senses]—
that is called 'seen,' 'heard,' 'cognized,' and 'known' (<s>mata</s>), respectively. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.75 //
<s>Paiśunya</s> (slander) is the speech of one with a defiled mind [aimed at] dividing others;

children.text: pārūṣyamapriyaṃ sarva kliṣṭaṃ bhinna pralāpitā // VAkK_4.76 //
children.translated_text: <s>pāruṣya</s> (harsh speech) is all unpleasant defiled [speech]; <s>sambhinnapralāpa</s> (idle chatter) is— // <s>VAkK</s> 4.76 //
according to others, any other defiled [speech]—like gossip, singing, and acting;
likewise from the wholesome [side]; but <s>abhidhyā</s> (covetousness) is the unjust desire for another's property. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.77 //
<s>Vyāpāda</s> (malice) is hatred toward beings; <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view) [denies] good and bad;

children.text: mithyādṛṣṭiḥ trayo hyatra panthānaḥ sapta karma ca // VAkK_4.78 //
