children.translated_text: [that is] wrong view; for here [in the ten unwholesome paths] there are three paths and seven actions. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.78 //
Cutting the root (<s>mūlaccheda</s>) [is done] by the wrong view, for those born in the desire realm who have obtained rebirth;
[it is] the view that denies results and causes—completely, gradually, among humans. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.79 //
A woman cuts [the root]; a man [cuts it]; one of view-conduct; that [cutting] is disconnection (<s>asam­anvaya</s>);
reconnection [comes] through doubt and the view of existence; not for one who commits an <s>ānantarya</s> (immediate retribution deed). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.80 //
Simultaneously, up to eight unwholesome [paths] occur together;
<s>cetanā</s> (volition) [operates] with up to ten; wholesome [paths]—not one, [nor] eight, [nor] five [simultaneously]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.81 //
Idle chatter, harsh speech, and malice [exist] in hell in two ways;
by way of possession (<s>samanvāgama</s>)—covetousness and wrong view; in <s>Kuru</s> [there are] three. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.82 //
The seventh [unwholesome path is present] here by itself too; in the desire [realm] elsewhere, [all] ten unwholesome [paths];
but three wholesome [paths are present] everywhere, through direct encounter and acquisition. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.83 //
Among beings in the formless realm and the unconscious (<s>asaṃjñisattva</s>) [realm]—seven by acquisition, the rest [excluded];
and also by direct encounter—excluding the hell-beings and <s>Kuru</s> [-dwellers]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.84 //
All [action-paths] are held to give <s>adhipati</s> (dominant), <s>niṣyanda</s> (outflow), and <s>vipāka</s> (maturation) results;
from inflicting suffering, killing, and destroying vitality—the threefold result. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.85 //
Bodily and verbal action born from greed is separately designated as <s>mithyājīva</s> (wrong livelihood);

children.text: duḥśodhatvāt pariṣkāralobhotthaṃ cet na sūtrataḥ // VAkK_4.86 //
children.translated_text: because it is difficult to purify; [but] if [wrong livelihood is merely] greed arising from accessories (<s>pariṣkāra</s>)—no, according to the <s>sūtras</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.86 //
On the path of abandonment, when defilements are equal (<s>samala</s>), action bears fruit through five [results];
through four when [defilements are] stainless (<s>amala</s>); and other defiled wholesome and unwholesome [action likewise]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.87 //

children.text: anāsravaṃ punaḥ śeṣaṃ tribhiravyākṛtaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: The undefiled [action], further, [gives] the remaining [results] through three; and that which is indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>)—

children.text: catvāri dve tathā trīṇi kuśalasya śubhādayaḥ // VAkK_4.88 //
children.translated_text: four, two, then three—[these are] the wholesome and other [results]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.88 //
For the unwholesome—wholesome and other [results in] two, three, four, in sequence;

children.text: avyākṛtasya dve trīṇi trīṇī caite śubhādayaḥ // VAkK_4.89 //
children.translated_text: for the indeterminate—two, three, three—these [are] the wholesome and other [results]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.89 //
For all that is past—four [results]; for the present also—the middle [results]; the future ones—

children.text: madhyamā dve ajātasya phalāni trīṇyanāgatāḥ // VAkK_4.90 //
children.translated_text: for the present—two; for the unborn—three results [are] future. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.90 //
Dharmas of one's own stage—four [results]; those of other stages—three or two;

children.text: śaikṣasya trīṇi śaikṣādyāḥ aśaikṣasya tu karmaṇaḥ // VAkK_4.91 //
children.translated_text: for a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>)—three: learner's [dharmas] etc.; but for the non-learner's (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) action— // <s>VAkK</s> 4.91 //

children.text: dharmāḥ śaikṣādikā ekaṃ phalaṃ trīṇyapi ca dvayam /
children.translated_text: dharmas [consisting of] learner's etc.—one result; three too and also two;

children.text: tābhyāmanyasya śaikṣādyā dve dve pañca phalāni ca // VAkK_4.92 //
children.translated_text: for [what belongs to] other than those two—learner's etc. [give] two, two, and five results. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.92 //

children.text: trīṇi catvāri caikaṃ ca dṛggheyasya tadādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Three, four, and one—for that abandoned by seeing (<s>dṛgheya</s>)—those and others;

children.text: te dve catvāryatha trīṇi bhāvanāheyakarmaṇaḥ // VAkK_4.93 //
children.translated_text: those [give] two, four, then three—for action abandoned by meditation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.93 //

children.text: apraheyasya te tvekaṃ dve catvāri yathākramam /
children.translated_text: For that which is not to be abandoned (<s>apraheya</s>)—those [give] one, two, four, in due order;

children.text: ayogavihitaṃ kliṣṭaṃ vidhibhraṣṭaṃ ca kecana // VAkK_4.94 //
children.translated_text: some [say that wrong livelihood is] the defiled [which is] not properly applied, or deviation from proper conduct. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.94 //
One [action] projects one birth; one [birth is] completed by many [supplementary actions];

children.text: nākṣepike samāpattī acitte prāptayo na ca // VAkK_4.95 //
children.translated_text: the two attainments (<s>samāpatti</s>) [of cessation and unconsciousness] are not projecting [actions]; nor [are] acquisitions (<s>prāpti</s>) in the mindless [states]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.95 //
The <s>ānantarya</s> actions (deeds of immediate retribution)—intense defilement, then bad destiny—
[and being a] <s>Kuru</s>-dweller, unconscious being—these are considered the three obstructions (<s>āvaraṇa</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.96 //

children.text: triṣu dvipeṣvānantarya śaṇḍhā dīnāṃ tu neṣyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>ānantarya</s> [deeds occur] in three continents; [those of] <s>śaṇḍhas</s> (eunuchs) and the wretched are not accepted—
because of their small capacity to benefit and their shamelessness; in the remaining five destinies— // <s>VAkK</s> 4.97 //
<s>saṃghabheda</s> (schism of the community) has the nature of non-concord (<s>asāmagrī</s>), [is] a <s>viprayukta</s> (dissociated) [dharma],
an undefiled-indeterminate dharma; the <s>saṅgha</s> is that [which is] connected with it. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.98 //
The blame for that [comes from] false speech; the schismatic is connected with it;

children.text: avīcau pacyate kalpam adhikairadhikā rujaḥ // VAkK_4.99 //
children.translated_text: he is tormented in <s>Avīci</s> for a <s>kalpa</s>; by additional [offenses], additional suffering. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.99 //

children.text: bhikṣurdṛk carito vṛttī bhinatti anyatra bāliśān /
children.translated_text: A <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), of view-conduct (<s>dṛṣṭicarita</s>), who engages [in schism]—splits [the saṅgha], except from fools;
when there is patience toward another path [and another] teacher—the split one does not submit to [authority]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.100 //

children.text: cakrabhedaḥ sa ca mataḥ jambūdvīpe navādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: That [schism] is considered 'wheel-schism' (<s>cakrabheda</s>), in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, by [a minimum of] nine [monks] and more;
'action-schism' (<s>karmabheda</s>) [occurs] in the three continents, by eight and more. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.101 //
At the beginning, at the end, before an <s>arbuda</s> [has elapsed], after a <s>yuga</s> [from the Teacher's departure], when the Sage has passed away,

children.text: sīmāyāṃ cāpyabaddhāyāṃ cakrabhedo na jāyate // VAkK_4.102 //
children.translated_text: and within an unestablished boundary (<s>sīmā</s>)—wheel-schism does not arise. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.102 //
Because of destroying [the Buddha's] benefit, qualities, field, and response to refutation—
[the ānantarya] may be intermediated by marks (<s>vyañjana</s>); the mother is she from whose blood [one is] born. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.103 //
For one who intends to strike the <s>Buddha</s>, from the blow [itself] he does not deserve [a higher stage];
nor is the attainment of the fruit of detachment possible for one engaged in an <s>ānantarya</s> deed. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.104 //
False speech [that causes] <s>saṃghabheda</s> is considered the most blameworthy (<s>mahāvadyatama</s>);
volition [directed toward] the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) is the most fruitful wholesome [deed] in the world. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.105 //
Corruption of one's mother, of a female <s>Arhat</s>, killing of one who is definitely established [on the path],
of a <s>bodhisattva</s>, of a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>)—[and] stealing the community's property— // <s>VAkK</s> 4.106 //
these are comparable to the <s>ānantarya</s> deeds; the fifth is the breaking of a <s>stūpa</s>;
[these] create great obstruction to the attainment of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience), <s>anāgāmitva</s> (non-returning), and <s>arhattva</s> (arhatship). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.107 //

children.text: bodhisattvaḥ kuto yāvat yato lakṣaṇa karmakṛt /
children.translated_text: From when [does] a <s>bodhisattva</s> [begin]? From when he performs the action of [acquiring] the marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>);
[reborn in] a good destiny, of good family, with unimpaired [faculties], male, remembering [past] births, irreversible. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.108 //
In <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, a man alone, directly before a <s>Buddha</s>, [generating] the intention;

children.text: cintāmayaṃ kalpaśate śeṣa ākṣipate hi tat // VAkK_4.109 //
children.translated_text: [the aspiration is] born of reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>); in a hundred <s>kalpas</s> the remainder [of merit] is projected. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.109 //
Each [mark] is born from a hundred [acts of] merit; the last of the three incalculable [aeons are under]:
<s>Vipaśyin</s>, <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, <s>Ratnaśikhin</s>—[and] formerly <s>Śākyamuni</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.110 //
Everywhere, [by] giving everything [to all], from compassion—the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>);
even when a limb is cut, from non-anger—[the perfection of] patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) and morality (<s>śīla</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.111 //
By the praise of <s>Tiṣya</s> [standing on one foot]—[the perfection of] vigor (<s>vīrya</s>); [the perfection of] wisdom (<s>dhī</s>) and <s>samādhi</s>—immediately [thereafter];

children.text: puṇyaṃ kriyātha tadvastu trayaṃ karmapathā yathā // VAkK_4.112 //
children.translated_text: merit is action; and its basis is threefold, like the action-paths. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.112 //
That by which [something] is given is <s>dāna</s> (giving)—from the desire to honor and benefit;

children.text: kāyavākkarma sotthānaṃ mahābhogyaphalaṃ ca tat // VAkK_4.113 //
children.translated_text: [it is] bodily and verbal action, together with its generation; and it has great enjoyment as its fruit. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.113 //
One gives for one's own benefit, another's benefit, both, or neither;
its distinction [arises] further from the distinction of the donor, the gift, and the recipient-field. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.114 //

children.text: dātā viśiṣṭaḥ śraddhādyaiḥ satkṛtyādi dadāti ataḥ /
children.translated_text: The donor is distinguished by faith and so forth; therefore he gives with respect, etc.;
[this means] respect, generosity, pleasure, [giving at the proper] time, [giving] without harming, and [proper] acquisition. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.115 //
The gift [is distinguished] by excellence of color and so forth—beauty, fame,
belovedness, softness, pleasantness of seasonal touch, and limb-endowment result therefrom. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.116 //
The [recipient-]field is distinguished by destiny, suffering, helpfulness, and qualities;

children.text: agraṃ muktasya muktāya bodhisattvasya ca aṣṭamam // VAkK_4.117 //
children.translated_text: the supreme [field is a gift] from a liberated one to a liberated one; and to a <s>bodhisattva</s> of the eighth [stage]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.117 //
To mother, father, the sick, a <s>Dharma</s>-preacher, and to one in his last birth—
to a <s>bodhisattva</s>—immeasurable [merit results]; even to non-noble persons the offering (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) [brings merit]. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.118 //
The support (<s>pṛṣṭha</s>), the field, the intention (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), the effort (<s>prayoga</s>), the volition (<s>cetanā</s>), and the disposition (<s>āśaya</s>)—
from the mild or intense [nature] of these, the action [is] mild or intense. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.119 //
By deliberate volition (<s>saṃcetanā</s>) and completion (<s>samāpti</s>), [and] from lack of remorse, from the opponent [side],
from retinue (<s>parivāra</s>) and from maturation (<s>vipāka</s>)—action is said to be 'accumulated' (<s>upacita</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.120 //
Merit in [giving to] a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) is in the lineage of renunciation; like <s>maitrī</s> and so forth, it does not [directly] seize [the recipient];
even in a poor field, there is a desirable result—because seed and fruit are not reversed. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.121 //
Immorality (<s>dauḥśīlya</s>) is unwholesome form; morality (<s>śīla</s>) is its abstention, twofold;

children.text: pratikṣiptācca buddhena viśuddhaṃ tu caturguṇam // VAkK_4.122 //
children.translated_text: and [that morality which is] ordained by the <s>Buddha</s>—the purified [morality] has four qualities. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.122 //
[It is] uninjured by immorality and its causes, supported by the opponent and by tranquility;

children.text: samāhitaṃ tu kuśalaṃ bhāvanā cittavāsanāt // VAkK_4.123 //
children.translated_text: but wholesome [action that is] concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>) is cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>)—from habituation of the mind. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.123 //
Morality is primarily for heaven; cultivation is for liberation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>);

children.text: caturṇāṃ brāhmapuṇyatvaṃ kalpaṃ svargeṣu modanāt // VAkK_4.124 //
children.translated_text: the four <s>brāhma</s> [meritorious bases have] the nature of merit—from enjoying [their fruit] in heavens for a <s>kalpa</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.124 //
The gift of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmadāna</s>) is the undefiled teaching of <s>sūtras</s> and so forth, in accordance with reality;
wholesome [action] is threefold: [leading to] merit, <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and penetration (<s>nirvedha</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 4.125 //
Action set in motion by practice (<s>yoga</s>), together with its generator, is threefold—

children.text: lipimudre sagaṇanaṃ kāvyaṃ saṃkhyā yathākramam // VAkK_4.126 //
children.translated_text: writing, seal-making, together with counting, poetry, and enumeration, respectively. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.126 //

children.text: sāvadyā nivṛtā hīnāḥ kliṣṭāḥ dharmāḥ śubhāmalāḥ /
children.translated_text: The blameworthy (<s>sāvadya</s>) dharmas are restrained, inferior, and defiled; the wholesome are stainless,
excellent; the conditioned wholesome [dharmas] are to be practiced; but <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) is unsurpassed. // <s>VAkK</s> 4.127 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, entitled 'Exposition on Action' (<s>Karmanirdeśa</s>). //

children.translated_text: The root of existence (<s>bhava</s>) [consists of] the <s>anuśayas</s> (latent defilements)—six: <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>pratigha</s> (aversion),

children.text: māno 'vidyā ca dṛṣṭiśca vicikitsā ca te punaḥ // VAkK_5.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>māna</s> (pride), <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>dṛṣṭi</s> (view), and <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt); they, again— // <s>VAkK</s> 5.1 //
from the division of <s>rāga</s> into six, seven are stated; <s>bhavarāga</s> (attachment to existence) arises in two realms;
[it is] separately designated because of its inward-turning nature, in order to counteract the notion of its liberation. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.2 //
The views (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) are five: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-aggregate), <s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s> (wrong view), <s>antagrāhadṛṣṭi</s> (extreme view),
<s>dṛṣṭiparāmarśa</s> (adherence to views), and <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (adherence to rites and vows)—thus, [the anuśayas are] again ten. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.3 //
These ten [are distributed as] seven, seven, eight—excluding three and two views [respectively];
they are abandoned in order by the seeings (<s>darśana</s>) of suffering and so forth in the desire realm. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.4 //
Four are abandoned by meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>); those same [ten], again, without <s>pratigha</s> (aversion),
[obtain] in the form realm, likewise in the formless realm—thus ninety-eight [anuśayas] are accepted. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.5 //
Those arising at the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>) are killed by <s>kṣānti</s> (acceptance)—[they are] abandoned by seeing alone; the rest—
by seeing and meditation; those not killed by <s>kṣānti</s>—by meditation alone. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.6 //

[The aspects of] <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> are: self (<s>ātma</s>), mine (<s>ātmīya</s>), permanent (<s>dhruva</s>), annihilation (<s>uccheda</s>), non-existence (<s>nāsti</s>), inferior (<s>hīna</s>)—these [characterize the] five views;
[asserting] a non-cause, a non-path, and the view of that—these are the five views. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.7 //
It operates [based on] the erroneous [notions] of permanence, self, etc., regarding <s>Īśvara</s> (God) and so forth;
adherence to [wrong] causes—therefore it is abandoned only by the seeing of suffering. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.8 //
From three views, the fourfold <s>viparyāsa</s> (inversion)—from what is inverted;

children.text: nitīraṇāt samāropāt saṃjñācitte tu tadvaśāt // VAkK_5.9 //
children.translated_text: [it is] of perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and thought (<s>citta</s>) through non-ascertainment and superimposition—[arising] under their influence. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.9 //
Seven [kinds of] <s>māna</s> (pride), ninefold; from the three—seeing, meditation, and destruction [come their abandonment];
<s>paryavasthāna</s> (manifest defilement) and so forth, from killing [onward]—these too are abandoned by meditation. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.10 //
The desire for non-existence (<s>vibhavecchā</s>) does not occur for a noble one (<s>ārya</s>); methods (<s>vidhi</s>) and so forth [also do not];

children.text: nāsmitā dṛṣṭipuṣṭatvāt kaukṛtyaṃ nāpi cāśubham // VAkK_5.11 //
children.translated_text: nor <s>asmitā</s> (self-conceit), because it is nourished by views; nor regret (<s>kaukṛtya</s>), nor the unwholesome. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.11 //
The universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>) [defilements] abandoned by seeing suffering and its cause [are]: the views, likewise

children.text: vimatiḥ saha tābhiśca yāvidyāveṇikī ca yā // VAkK_5.12 //
children.translated_text: doubt, and the <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) that accompanies them and that which is specific [to each truth]. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.12 //
Nine have higher [stages] as object—excluding the two views;
excluding acquisition (<s>prāpti</s>); those that co-arise [with them], [and] those also connected with them—these too are universal. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.13 //
Wrong view, doubt, the ignorance conjoined with them, and isolated [ignorance]—
those abandoned by seeing cessation and the path—six [defilements] have undefiled [dharmas] as object. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.14 //
The tranquility (<s>uparama</s>) of one's own stage is the path; [the path operates in] six stages and nine stages;
the domain of those [defilements] having that [path] as object—for the path is different, having another as cause. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.15 //
There is no <s>rāga</s> [toward nirodha and mārga], because they are to be abandoned; no <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred), because they do no harm;

children.text: na māno na parāmarśau śāntaśuddhyagrabhāvataḥ // VAkK_5.16 //
children.translated_text: no <s>māna</s>, no <s>parāmarśas</s> (adherences)—because of [their] peaceful, pure, and supreme nature. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.16 //
The universal (<s>sarvatraga</s>) <s>anuśayas</s> underlie (<s>anuśerate</s>) all [dharmas];
[they underlie] their own stage and object; the non-universal [defilements underlie] their own category (<s>nikāya</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 5.17 //
They do not [underlie] the undefiled or what has a higher [stage] as object—because of non-acceptance and because of being the opponent;

children.text: yena yaḥ saṃprayuktastu sa tasmin saṃprayogataḥ // VAkK_5.18 //
children.translated_text: but whatever [defilement] is conjoined with whatever [dharma]—that [defilement underlies] that [dharma] through conjunction. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.18 //
Above [the desire realm], all [anuśayas] are indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>); in the desire realm, <s>satkāyadarśana</s> (personality-view),

children.text: antagrāhaḥ sahābhyāṃ ca mohaḥ śeṣāstvihāśubhāḥ // VAkK_5.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>antagrāha</s> (extreme view), together with the <s>moha</s> (delusion) [accompanying] those two—the rest here are unwholesome. // <s>VAkK</s> 5.19 //
In the desire realm, the unwholesome roots are passion, aversion, and delusion;
These three unwholesome roots are craving, ignorance, and [wrong] view. // 5.20 //
Because of the twofold upward operation, no other [roots exist]; the outsiders assert only four —
Craving, [wrong] view, pride, and delusion — [the last] because of its contemplative nature, [they consider it] as ignorance. // 5.21 //
A categorical declaration, [or] an answer by distinguishing, or by a counter-question,
Or by setting aside — [these four types apply to questions about] death and birth, the self distinguished [from what is] other, and so forth. // 5.22 //
Through passion, aversion, and pride — past and present —
Where [a latent affliction] has arisen and is not abandoned, in that object one is fettered. // 5.23 //
Everywhere, by future [afflictions], by mental [afflictions], by those of one's own time-period and by others',

children.text: ajaiḥ sarvatra śeṣaistu sarvaiḥ sarvatra saṃyutaḥ // VAkK_5.24 //
children.translated_text: By those unborn, one is fettered everywhere; but by the remaining [afflictions], one is fettered everywhere by all. // 5.24 //
The existence of all times [is established] because it has been stated, because of the two [conditions], because of a real object, and because of a result;
Because of the assertion of their existence, they are called <s>Sarvāstivādins</s>; they are of four kinds. // 5.25 //
They are designated by essential nature, by characteristic, by state, and by alteration;

children.text: tṛtīyaḥ śobhanaḥ adhvānaḥ kāritreṇa vyavasthitāḥ // VAkK_5.26 //
children.translated_text: The third is excellent: the time-periods are established by [their] function. // 5.26 //

children.text: kiṃ vighnaṃ tatkathaṃ nānyat adhvāyogaḥ tathā sataḥ /
children.translated_text: What is the obstacle? How is nothing else [an obstacle]? Likewise, the connection with time-periods of an existent —

children.text: ajātanaṣṭatā kena gambhīrā khalu dharmatā // VAkK_5.27 //
children.translated_text: By what [is there] the state of being unborn and destroyed? Profound indeed is the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. // 5.27 //
When the [afflictions] to be abandoned by seeing suffering are abandoned, one is still fettered by the remaining universal [afflictions];

children.text: prāk prahīṇe prakare ca śeṣaistadviṣayairmalaiḥ // VAkK_5.28 //
children.translated_text: When the earlier [category] is abandoned, and also the [next] group, [one is fettered] by the remaining defilements having that object. // 5.28 //
Those to be abandoned by seeing suffering and its origin, arising in the desire realm through practice,
Have as their domain their own three [realms], one [realm] of form, and consciousness free from defilement. // 5.29 //
Those arising in the form realm [have as domain] their own, the lower three, the upper one, and the defilements;
Those arising in the formless realm [have as domain] the three realms and [things that are] defilement-free. // 5.30 //
Those to be abandoned by seeing cessation and the path — all have as domain their own and what is above;
The defilement-free [domain] of the three realms, the final three, and the defilement-free. // 5.31 //
That which has latent afflictions is twofold — defiled and undefiled, [but both] accompanied by latent afflictions;
First delusion, then doubt; from that, wrong view; from that, the view of self; // 5.32 //
From that, the view of the extremes; from that, adherence to rules and morality; from that, view;

children.text: rāgaḥ svadṛṣṭau mānaśca dveṣo 'nyatra ityanukramaḥ // VAkK_5.33 //
children.translated_text: Passion toward one's own view; pride; and aversion toward others — this is the order. // 5.33 //
From an unabandoned latent affliction, from its object, from a present [stimulus],
And from improper mental attention — the complete cause of an affliction [arising]. // 5.34 //
In the desire realm, the afflictions with their secondary afflictions — excluding delusion — are the <s>kāmāsrava</s> (outflow of desire) as latent afflictions;

children.text: mohena anuśayā eva rūpārūpye bhavāsravaḥ // VAkK_5.35 //
children.translated_text: In the form and formless realms, [they constitute] the <s>bhavāsrava</s> (outflow of existence). // 5.35 //
Because they are morally neutral, inward-directed, and belong to the meditative levels,
Therefore they are unified [as one outflow]; the root is ignorance — hence [it is] a separate outflow. // 5.36 //
Likewise the floods and yokes; but the views are set apart because of their acuteness;
Among the defilement-free, those without companions have no conformity with [the outflows]. // 5.37 //
The outflows as stated, together with ignorance, are twofold through the separation of views;

children.text: upādānāni avidyā tu grāhikā ne ti miśritā // VAkK_5.38 //
children.translated_text: The clingings — but ignorance, since it grasps, is not [listed separately]; it is mixed in. // 5.38 //
These are called atomic and latent; they are latent in two ways;
Because they bind, they are called <s>anuśayas</s> (latent afflictions). // 5.39 //
They lie dormant, they flow out, they carry away, they bind together,
And they seize — these are the etymologies of <s>āsrava</s> (outflow) and the rest. // 5.40 //
Through the division of fetters and so forth, they are further stated as fivefold;
A fetter different [from the views] — through the material [aspect], adherence, and generality of views. // 5.41 //
Because it is exclusively unwholesome, and because both [jealousy and miserliness] are autonomous,
Jealousy and miserliness are stated among these as a separate pair of fetters. // 5.42 //
Fivefold are the fetters of the lower part: by two [fetters], there is no transcendence of the desire [realm];
By three, there is return [to desire realm]; the three are from grasping at entry, root, and [false] view. // 5.43 //
Not going to the [higher], desire for the desire realm, confusion about the path, doubt about the path —
These are the obstacles to liberation in the journey; hence the threefold teaching. // 5.44 //
Fivefold are the fetters of the upper part: the two passions — those born of form and formless [realms],
Restlessness, pride, and delusion — the three bonds, by definition. // 5.45 //
Other mental factors that are defiled, designated as belonging to the aggregate of formations,
Are secondary afflictions derived from the afflictions — but they are not designated as afflictions [proper]. // 5.46 //
Shamelessness, recklessness, jealousy, miserliness, restlessness,
Remorse, sloth, and torpor — [these are] the eight secondary afflictions. // 5.47 //
Anger and concealment arise from passion; shamelessness, restlessness, and miserliness [also];
Concealment [also arises] from dispute; from ignorance [arise] sloth, torpor, and recklessness. // 5.48 //
Remorse from doubt; anger and jealousy follow from aversion;

children.text: anye ca ṣaṭkleśamalāḥ māyā śāṭhyaṃ madastathā // VAkK_5.49 //
children.translated_text: And the other six defilements of affliction: deceit, fraudulence, intoxication, // 5.49 //
Hostility, resentment, and harmfulness — of these, deceit and intoxication arise from passion;
Resentment and harmfulness arise from aversion. // 5.50 //
Hostility from adherence to views; fraudulence arises from [wrong] view;
Among these, shamelessness, recklessness, sloth, torpor, and restlessness are each twofold. // 5.51 //
Others [of these secondary afflictions] are to be abandoned by cultivation; they are autonomous and [also] defilements;
In the desire [realm], three are unwholesome in two ways; beyond [desire realm], they are morally neutral. // 5.52 //
Deceit and fraudulence — in the desire realm and up to the first two <s>dhyānas</s>, because of deceiving <s>Brahmā</s>;
Sloth, restlessness, and intoxication exist in all three realms; the others arise only in the desire realm. // 5.53 //
Those established simultaneously, to be abandoned by seeing, belong to the mental consciousness level;

children.text: upakleśāḥ svatantrāśca ṣaḍ vijñānāśrayāḥ pare // VAkK_5.54 //
children.translated_text: The secondary afflictions are autonomous; the remaining [secondary ones] are based in the six consciousnesses. // 5.54 //

children.text: sukhābhyāṃ saṃprayukto hi rāgaḥ dveṣo viparyayāt /
children.translated_text: Passion is associated with the two pleasant [feelings]; aversion with the opposite;
Delusion with all; wrong view with mental suffering and pleasure. // 5.55 //
Doubt [is associated] with displeasure; the others [in the desire realm] with joy;
All are also [associated] with equanimity; those of the higher levels [associate] with their own respective [feelings]. // 5.56 //
With displeasure: remorse, jealousy, anger, harmfulness,

children.text: upanāhaḥ pradāśaśca mātsaryaṃ tu viparyayāt // VAkK_5.57 //
children.translated_text: Resentment, and hostility; miserliness with the opposite. // 5.57 //

children.text: māyā śāṭhyamatho mrakṣo middhaṃ cobhayathā madaḥ /
children.translated_text: Deceit, fraudulence, concealment, and torpor [are associated] with both; intoxication
With the two pleasant [feelings]; universal equanimity; the [remaining] four with the five [feelings]. // 5.58 //
In the desire realm, the hindrances [are so designated] from their function as opponents, sustenance, and action of each single [hindrance];
The pair-nature, the fivefold [nature] — from obstructing the aggregates and from doubt. // 5.59 //
From the full knowledge of the object, from the exhaustion of that object,
From the abandonment of the object, and from the arising of the antidote — [comes] cessation. // 5.60 //
The antidote is fourfold: as the basis of abandonment, as the so-called destroyer,

children.text: pratipakṣaḥ prahātavyaḥ kleśa ālambanāt mataḥ // VAkK_5.61 //
children.translated_text: [As direct opponent, and as the thing] to be abandoned — the affliction is considered [abandoned] from its object. // 5.61 //
Due to difference in nature, opposition, separation by place and time,
Like the distance of elements, morality, region, and time-periods — the two are [truly] far apart. // 5.62 //
Once-for-all cessation — the attainment of disconnection — [occurs] for them again and again
Through the arising of the antidote, the attainment of its result, and the development of the faculties. // 5.63 //
Full knowledges are nine: the desire [realm] and the rest — the exhaustion of the two kinds of each category;

children.text: ekā dvayoḥ kṣaye dve te tathordhvaṃ tisra eva tāḥ // VAkK_5.64 //
children.translated_text: One at the exhaustion of two; two of them; and above, exactly three. // 5.64 //
The other [three] are the exhaustion of the lower-part [fetters], the form [realm afflictions], and all outflows —

children.text: tisraḥ parijñāḥ ṣaṭ kṣāntiphalaṃ jñānasya śeṣitāḥ // VAkK_5.65 //
children.translated_text: Three full knowledges; the six are the result of <s>kṣānti</s> (patience); the remaining are of knowledge. // 5.65 //
The result of the <s>anāgamya</s> (preliminary meditation) is all [full knowledges]; or five of the <s>dhyānas</s>;
Eight of the <s>sāmantaka</s> (preliminary); one each of the principal and the three formless [attainments]. // 5.66 //

children.text: āryamārgasya sarvāḥ dve laukikasya anvayasya ca /
children.translated_text: Of the noble path, all; two of the worldly path; likewise of the subsequent [knowledge];

children.text: dharmajñānasya tisrastu ṣaṭ tatpakṣasya pañca ca // VAkK_5.67 //
children.translated_text: Three of <s>dharma</s>-knowledge; six of its counterpart; and five. // 5.67 //
From the attainment of separation from the defilement-free, from the impairment of the summit of existence,
From the destruction of the two causes, full knowledge [arises] from transcending the realm. // 5.68 //
One who is at the stage of seeing is accompanied by up to five, through a single [full knowledge];

children.text: bhāvanāsthaḥ punaḥ ṣaḍibharekayā vā dvayena vā // VAkK_5.69 //
children.translated_text: One at the stage of cultivation — by six, or by one, or by two. // 5.69 //
Their combination [occurs] from the attainment of detachment from a realm and the obtaining of a result;

children.text: ekāṃ dve pañca ṣaṭ kaścijjahātyāpnoti pañca na // VAkK_5.70 //
children.translated_text: Someone abandons one, two, five, or six, and does not obtain five. // 5.70 //

body.translated_text: Here ends the discussion of full knowledge.
The fifth chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, the Exposition of Latent Afflictions, is completed.
Whatever merit [accrues] herein to the venerable <s>Lāmāvāka</s>.

children.translated_text: The abandonment of afflictions has been declared — from seeing the truths and from cultivation;
The path of cultivation is twofold; that called 'seeing' is exclusively supramundane. // 6.1 //
Four truths have been stated: suffering, origin,

children.text: nirodhamārga iti eṣāṃ yathābhisamayaṃ kramaḥ // VAkK_6.2 //
children.translated_text: Cessation, and the path — their order corresponds to [the order of] realization. // 6.2 //
Suffering — from connection with the three kinds of suffering, in all respects, without remainder;

children.text: manāpā amanāpāśca tadanye caiva sāsravāḥ // VAkK_6.3 //
children.translated_text: The agreeable and the disagreeable, and what is other than those — [all] that is with outflows. // 6.3 //

children.text: yatra bhinnena tadbuddhiranyāpohe dhiyā ca tat /
children.translated_text: That which, when broken, the cognition [of it] ceases; and that which [is cognized] by the exclusion of others —
The former is conventionally real, like a pot or water; the latter is ultimately real. // 6.4 //
One established in moral conduct, possessing learning and reflection, applies to cultivation;
The wisdoms beginning with that born of hearing have as their object names, both [name and meaning], and meaning [respectively]. // 6.5 //
Without the two withdrawals; not of discontent and great desire;
Contentment is satisfaction with what is obtained, wishing for more; great desire is wanting what is not obtained. // 6.6 //
From perversion, [arise] the opposites of those two; the two are obtained from the three realms, free from defilement;
Non-attachment — the noble lineages, of which three are of the nature of contentment. // 6.7 //
Conduct [operates] through the three [doors of] action; as the antidote to the arising of craving;
For the cessation — temporal and final — of one's desire for possessions, self, and objects. // 6.8 //
The entry into that [path is] through the meditation on the impure and through mindfulness of breathing;
As a remedy for those of excessive passion and excessive discursive thought; all those with passion [benefit]. // 6.9 //
From the ocean-of-bones to the expansion and contraction — [this is] for the beginner;
From the foot-bone through the abandonment of half the skull — one is said to have attained mastery. // 6.10 //
The contemplation of the transcendent [stage] is through fixing the mind between the eyebrows;
Non-attachment has ten stages; the impure [meditation] has as object desire-realm and visible [forms]. // 6.11 //
Mindfulness of breathing is wisdom; it has five stages; its object is wind moving [in and out];

children.text: kāmāśrayā na bāhyānām ṣaḍ vidhā gaṇanādibhiḥ // VAkK_6.12 //
children.translated_text: It is based in the desire realm; it does not apply to external [winds]; it is sixfold through counting and so forth. // 6.12 //
In-breathing and out-breathing — because the body [is involved]; they are called 'belonging to a being'; they are unappropriated;

children.text: naiḥṣyandikau nādhareṇa lakṣyete manasā ca tau // VAkK_6.13 //
children.translated_text: They are naturally resultant; they are not [apprehended] below; they are observed by the mind. // 6.13 //
Having accomplished <s>śamatha</s> (calm), one should cultivate the <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) —
Through the examination of the two characteristics of body, feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>. // 6.14 //
Wisdom born of hearing and the rest; others [say they are distinguished] by association and object; the sequence
Is according to arising; but the fourfold [division] is as an antidote to the [four] perversions. // 6.15 //
Established in the foundation of mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s>, with all [four truths] as object,
One contemplates them as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, and as non-self. // 6.16 //
Then arise the <s>ūṣmagatas</s> (warmth stages); they have the four truths as their object,

children.text: ṣoḍaśākāram ūṣmabhyo mūrdhānaḥ te 'pi tādṛśāḥ // VAkK_6.17 //
children.translated_text: With sixteen aspects; from the warmth stages [arise] the <s>mūrdhānas</s> (peaks); they are of the same nature. // 6.17 //
Reduction to [a single] <s>dharma</s>-aspect [is possible]; but increase also by other [aspects];

children.text: tebhyaḥ kṣāntiḥ dvidhā tadvat kṣāntyā dharmeṇa vardhanam // VAkK_6.18 //
children.translated_text: From those [arise] the <s>kṣāntis</s> (patiences), twofold, of the same nature; from patience, increase [occurs] through the <s>dharma</s>-aspect. // 6.18 //
Having the suffering of the desire realm as object, the supreme [patience] is momentary;

children.text: tathāgradharmāḥ sarve tu pañcaskandhāḥ vināptibhiḥ // VAkK_6.19 //
children.translated_text: Likewise the <s>agradharmāḥ</s> (supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s>); all are the five aggregates, excluding attainments. // 6.19 //
Thus the aids to penetration are fourfold, born of cultivation,

children.text: anāgamyā ntaradhyānabhūmikam dve tvadho 'pi vā // VAkK_6.20 //
children.translated_text: Belonging to the level of <s>anāgamya</s> and the intermediate <s>dhyānas</s>; or [the first] two may also be lower. // 6.20 //
Based in the desire realm, [the first two]; a woman obtains the supreme <s>dharmas</s> based in both [levels];
The noble one loses them through abandonment of the level; the non-noble through death. // 6.21 //

children.text: ādye dve parihāṇyā ca maulestatraiva satyadṛk /
children.translated_text: The first two [may be lost] through deterioration also; the principal [meditation] — therein the seer of truth;
A novel attainment; among the deficient, loss — the two are non-possession. // 6.22 //
The attainer of the peaks does not cut the root; the attainer of patience does not [go to] the lower realms;

children.text: śiṣyagotrā nnivartya dve buddhaḥ syāt trīṇyapītaraḥ // VAkK_6.23 //
children.translated_text: From the disciple-lineage, not turning back from two, one may become a <s>Buddha</s>; others from three or more. // 6.23 //
Until enlightenment, [one practices] everything in one [place]; at the end of <s>dhyāna</s>, for the Teacher and the rhinoceros-like [<s>pratyekabuddha</s>];
before those [stages], the [roots] conducive to liberation (<s>mokṣabhāgīya</s>) [arise]; liberation [comes] quickly, in three existences.
[Roots] born of hearing and reflection, three [types of] actions, are produced among humans;
from worldly [roots], up to the supreme <s>dharmas</s> (<s>agradharma</s>), the <s>dharmakṣānti</s> (patience toward dharma) is undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>).
Regarding suffering in the desire realm (<s>kāma</s>), then here itself, <s>dharmajñāna</s> (dharma-knowledge), and likewise again
regarding the remaining suffering, <s>anvayakṣānti</s> (subsequent patience) and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge); similarly for the [other] three truths.
Thus this realization of the truths (<s>satyābhisamaya</s>) consists of sixteen mind-moments and is threefold:
called seeing (<s>darśana</s>), object (<s>ālambana</s>), and function (<s>kārya</s>); it belongs to a single stage—that of the supreme <s>dharmas</s>.
<s>Kṣānti</s> (patience) and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) [moments] are, in order, the unimpeded path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) and the path of liberation (<s>muktimārga</s>);
the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) is for one who has not [yet] seen the [truths]; therein, fifteen moments [constitute it].
Those of dull and sharp faculties among them are the <s>śraddhānusārin</s> (faith-follower) and the <s>dharmānusārin</s> (dharma-follower);
they have not abandoned what is to be abandoned by meditation (<s>bhāvanāheya</s>), and are on the path to the first fruit (<s>phala</s>).
Up to [those who have] destroyed five types [of fetters], in the second [fruit], from the non-destruction of nine [types];
detached from the desire realm or above, they are on the path to the third [fruit].

children.text: ṣoḍaśe tu phalasthau tau yatra yaḥ pratipannakaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the sixteenth [moment], they are established in the fruit—in whichever [fruit] one is a candidate (<s>pratipannaka</s>);
[they become] <s>śraddhādhimukta</s> (faith-liberated) and <s>dṛṣṭyāpta</s> (view-attainer), [respectively], those of dull and sharp faculties.
For one established in a [lower] fruit, the attainment of a path superior to that fruit does not exist; therefore
one established in a fruit who is not [actively] engaged [in practice] is not a candidate for distinction.

children.text: navaprakārā doṣā hi bhūmau bhūmau tathā guṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: The faults (<s>doṣa</s>) in each stage are of nine types, and likewise the qualities (<s>guṇa</s>);
through the subdivision of mild, medium, and strong into further mild [medium, and strong] [sub-categories].
One established in the [first] fruit who has not [yet] destroyed what is to be abandoned by meditation is at most a <s>saptakṛtparama</s> (seven-times returner);
one who has freed three or four types is one of two or three births—a <s>kulaṃkula</s> (family-to-family).
Up to [one who has] destroyed five types, [he is] a candidate for the second fruit;
one who has exhausted the sixth type, that one is a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner).
One who has exhausted the seventh or eighth portion of faults, of one birth, is an <s>ekavīcika</s> (one-interval);
and a candidate for the third [fruit]; from the destruction of [all] nine, he is an <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner).
He [can be one who attains] <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state (<s>antarā</s>), at birth (<s>utpanna</s>), with effort (<s>sasaṃskāra</s>), or without effort (<s>asaṃskāra</s>);
and one who goes upward (<s>ūrdhvasrotas</s>); in <s>dhyāna</s>, one who is of mixed [attainments], going to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>;
he is a leaper (<s>pluta</s>), a half-leaper, one who dies from all [levels]; another goes to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>);
another who goes to the formless realm (<s>ārūpya</s>) is fourfold; another attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> here [in this life].
Again, making those [non-returners] each threefold, nine are said to be reborn in the form realm (<s>rūpopaga</s>);
the distinction among them is due to distinctions in <s>karma</s>, afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), and faculties (<s>indriya</s>).
By the subdivision of <s>ūrdhvasrotas</s> (one going upward), seven good destinies (<s>sadgati</s>) are recognized;
through good and bad conduct, non-conduct, going, and non-returning.
A noble one (<s>ārya</s>) whose birth is not reversed [does not return] to the desire realm; one reborn between realms (<s>dhātvantaropaga</s>)—
he who also goes upward does not partake of the decline of sense-faculties.
The fourth [<s>dhyāna</s>] is filled first, before the completion-moment, due to mixing;
for the purpose of rebirth and abiding, and also out of fear of afflictions.
Due to its fivefoldness, there are five types of rebirth in the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes);
a non-returner who has attained cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is further considered a <s>kāyasākṣin</s> (body-witness).
Up to the summit of existence, one who has destroyed the eighth portion, a candidate for <s>arhatship</s>;
on the unimpeded path of the ninth [stage] as well, that is the <s>vajropama</s> (diamond-like) [concentration].
From the attainment of the destruction of that [last portion], there is <s>kṣayajñāna</s> (knowledge of destruction); one who is beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), an <s>arhat</s>—that is he then.

children.text: lokottareṇa vairāgyaṃ bhavāgrāt anyato dvidhā // VAkK_6.45 //
children.translated_text: Dispassion from the summit of existence is by the supramundane [path]; from elsewhere, it is twofold.
In the noble's dispassion by the mundane [path], the attainments of disconnection (<s>visaṃyoga</s>) are twofold;
and by the supramundane—so some [hold]; because when afflictions are abandoned, there is no further connection.
One liberated from the lower [realms] up to the summit of existence has the status of one born above;
by the undefiled [path], dispassion from the non-returner stage onward [is] from all [levels].
From the <s>dhyāna</s> or from its preparatory stage (<s>sāmantaka</s>), the final path of liberation; in three stages of mastery;
from above the preparatory stages, by noble ones, with eight [types], victories over one's own and higher stages.
The paths of liberation and unimpeded paths that are mundane, in order,
have aspects of calm (<s>śānta</s>) etc. and of noble (<s>udāra</s>) etc.; they have higher and lower objects.
If [one asks] whether the [arhat] is unshakable (<s>akopya</s>)—from the knowledge of destruction, the thought 'there is no further arising' [comes]; but not [always].

children.text: kṣayajñānamaśaikṣo vā dṛṣṭiḥ sarvasya sārhataḥ // VAkK_6.50 //
children.translated_text: The knowledge of destruction is either that of a trainee-beyond (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) or a [complete] view—that of the <s>arhat</s>.
<s>Śrāmaṇya</s> (the state of an ascetic) is the stainless path; the fruit is both conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>);
there are ninety-one of those—the paths of liberation together with the knowledges of destruction.
The establishment of four fruits is due to five causes:
the prior abandonment, the attainment of another path, the destruction, and the combination regarding the fruit.
Then the attainment of eight knowledges, and the cultivation of sixteen aspects;

children.text: laukikāptaṃ tu miśratvānāsravāptiḥ dhṛteḥ phalam // VAkK_6.53 //
children.translated_text: but what is attained mundanely is mixed; the attainment of the undefiled is the fruit of steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>).
Brahminhood, the Brahma-wheel—that itself [is so called] because of the turning of Brahma;
the <s>Dharmacakra</s> (Wheel of Dharma) however is the path of seeing, from swiftness of movement etc., from the noble ones etc.

children.text: kāme trayāptiḥ antyasya triṣu nordhva hi dṛkpathaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the desire realm, attainment of three [fruits]; of the last [fruit], in three [realms]; but the path of seeing does not [operate] above;

children.text: asaṃvegādiha vidhā tatra niṣṭheti cāgamāt // VAkK_6.55 //
children.translated_text: due to lack of urgency here—there are [different] types; and "there is completion [only] there"—so says the <s>Āgama</s>.
Six types of <s>arhats</s> are recognized; five of them arise from <s>śraddhādhimukti</s> (faith-liberation);
their liberation is temporal (<s>sāmayikī</s>); [they are] of shaker-nature and unshakable-nature.
Therefore [the sixth] is the one liberated not-by-occasion; that one is identical with the <s>dṛṣṭiprāpta</s> (view-attainer).
Some of those [six] are [so] from the beginning by family-type (<s>gotra</s>); some arrive [there] through exertion (<s>uttāpana</s>).
From the family-type, decline is from four or five [types of arhat], not from the previous [level];

children.text: śaikṣānāryāśca ṣaḍgotrāḥ saṃcāro nāsti darśane // VAkK_6.58 //
children.translated_text: trainees (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and other noble ones are of six family-types; there is no transition in the path of seeing.
Decline (<s>parihāṇi</s>) should be known as threefold: from what is attained, from what is not [yet] attained, and from enjoyment;

children.text: antyā śāsturakopyasya madhyā cānyasya tu tridhā // VAkK_6.59 //
children.translated_text: the last [applies] to the Teacher and the unshakable [arhat]; the middle also to others—thus threefold.

children.text: mriyate na phalabhraṣṭaḥ tadakārya karoti na /
children.translated_text: One who has fallen from a fruit does not die [in that state]; nor does he perform its contrary action;
the paths of liberation and unimpeded paths—nine for the unshakable [arhat]—through repeated practice.
In the view-attainer, one by one, [the faculties are] undefiled; among humans there is growth;

children.text: aśaikṣo nava niśritya bhūmīḥ śaikṣastu ṣaṭ yataḥ // VAkK_6.61 //
children.translated_text: the one beyond training relies on nine stages; but the trainee on six, because—
abandoning a fruit with distinction, one attains the [same] fruit [of the higher type] by growth.

children.text: dvau buddhau śrāvakāḥ sapta navaite navadhendriyāḥ // VAkK_6.62 //
children.translated_text: Two <s>Buddhas</s>, seven <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers)—these nine have nine [controlling] faculties.
Through practice-effort, sense-attainment, [concentration-] attainment, and liberation—from both sides [they are] established;

children.text: pudgalāḥ sapta ṣaṭ tvete dvau dvau mārgatraye yataḥ // VAkK_6.63 //
children.translated_text: the [noble] persons are seven; but these are six, since two [pairs are counted as] two each, because of [the distinction of] three paths.
One liberated through cessation-attainment (<s>nirodha</s>) is liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayatovimukta</s>); the other, through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>);
one endowed with attainments, faculties, and fruits is called a full trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>).
Fullness of the state beyond training is due to two [things]; the path, in summary,
is fourfold, called: distinctive, liberating, unimpeded, and preparatory.
The path [operates] in the <s>dhyānas</s>; for one whose practice is pleasant, difficult in other stages;
for one of dull mind, <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge) [is attained] slowly; for the other, swiftly.
The knowledges of non-arising and of destruction [constitute] <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment); conforming to that,

children.text: saptatriṃśattu tatpakṣyāḥ nāmato dravyato daśa // VAkK_6.67 //
children.translated_text: there are thirty-seven factors on its side (<s>bodhipakṣya</s>); by name [thirty-seven], but in substance (<s>dravya</s>), ten.

children.text: śraddhā vīryaṃ smṛtiḥ prajñā samādhiḥ prītyupekṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: Faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>),
tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), and intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>)—wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is the foundation of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>);
vigor is called right exertion (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>); concentration [constitutes] the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>);

children.text: pradhānagrahaṇaṃ sarve guṇāḥ prāyogikāstu te // VAkK_6.69 //
children.translated_text: [each is so named from] the principal [factor]; all the qualities [belong to] the preparatory [stage].
They are cultivated in the stages of a beginner and of the penetration-conducive [roots];

children.text: bhāvane darśane caiva sapta vargā yathākramam // VAkK_6.70 //
children.translated_text: in the cultivation [path] and the seeing [path], the seven groups [are assigned] in order.
The factors of enlightenment (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>) and the path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>) are undefiled; the others are twofold;

children.text: sakalāḥ prathame dhyāne anāgamye prītivarjitāḥ // VAkK_6.71 //
children.translated_text: all [factors are present] in the first <s>dhyāna</s>; in the access [concentration], [all] except joy (<s>prīti</s>).
In the second [<s>dhyāna</s>], all except intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>); in those two, [all] minus those two respectively;

children.text: dhyānāntare ca śīlāṅgaistābhyāṃ ca triṣvarūpiṣu // VAkK_6.72 //
children.translated_text: and in the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s>, with the morality-factors; with those two also in the three formless [stages].
In the desire realm and at the summit of existence, the enlightenment- and path-factors are absent;
in the seeing of three truths, morality and the dharma-and-verified-confidence (<s>āvetyaprasāda</s>)—
are attained; at the realization of the path, also [confidence] in the <s>Buddha</s> and his <s>Saṅgha</s>;
"<s>Dharma</s>" [here means] the three truths; for <s>bodhisattvas</s> and <s>pratyekabuddhas</s>,

children.text: mārgaśca dravyatastu dve śraddhā śīlaṃ ca nirmalāḥ /
children.translated_text: also the path; but in substance these are two—faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and morality (<s>śīla</s>)—stainless.

children.text: noktā vimuktiḥ śaikṣāṅgaṃ baddhatvāt sā punardvidhā // VAkK_6.75 //
children.translated_text: Liberation is not mentioned as a trainee's factor, because it is [still] bound; it is again twofold:
the unconditioned [liberation] is the abandonment of afflictions; but the conditioned [is] conviction (<s>adhimukta</s>);

children.text: sāṅgaḥ saiva vimuktī dve jñānaṃ bodhiryathoditā // VAkK_6.76 //
children.translated_text: with its factors, that itself [constitutes] two liberations; knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is <s>bodhi</s> as stated.
A trainee's mind, being born, is liberated from the covering (<s>āvṛti</s>);
but the path, while ceasing, abandons that covering.
The unconditioned alone is called the element (<s>dhātu</s>); dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) is the exhaustion of passion (<s>rāga</s>);
the element of abandonment (<s>prahāṇadhātu</s>) pertains to the others; but [the element] called cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) pertains to entities.
One becomes disgusted through patience and knowledge of suffering and its cause; one becomes dispassionate
through all [knowledges]; one abandons by those—thus the fourfold conjunction arises.

body.text: abhidharmakośe mārgapudgalanirdeśo nāma ṣaṣṭhaṃ kośasthānaṃ samāptamiti //
body.translated_text: In the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, the sixth chapter (<s>kośasthāna</s>), entitled "Exposition of the Path and Persons" (<s>Mārgapudgalanirdeśa</s>), is completed.

children.translated_text: The stainless [knowledges are] the <s>kṣāntis</s> (patiences), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), the cognition of destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>) and non-arising (<s>anutpāda</s>)—not worldly;

children.text: tadanyobhayathāryā dhīḥ anyā jñānaṃ dṛśaśca ṣaṭ // VAkK_7.1 //
children.translated_text: noble cognition (<s>āryā dhī</s>) is of both kinds otherwise; other [worldly cognition] is knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) and seeing (<s>dṛś</s>)—the six [types].
Knowledge is [both] defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>) and undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>); the first is the indicator of conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛtijñāpaka</s>);
the undefiled is twofold: <s>dharmajñāna</s> (dharma-knowledge) and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge).
The conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) has all objects; <s>dharmajñāna</s> has suffering etc. in the desire realm as its object;
<s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge) has suffering etc. in the upper [realms] as its object.

children.text: te eva satyabhedena catvāri ete caturvidhe /
children.translated_text: Those same [knowledges], by the division of truths, are four; and these, in the fourfold [analysis],
[include] the knowledges of non-arising and destruction; those again [arise] from the first-mentioned.
From the subsequent knowledge of suffering and its cause, from the four [knowledges comes] the knowledge of others' minds (<s>paracittajñāna</s>);

children.text: bhūmyakṣapudgalotkrāntaṃ naṣṭājātaṃ na vetti tat // VAkK_7.5 //
children.translated_text: it does not know what has transcended stage, faculty, or person, nor what is lost, nor what is unborn.
It is of the class of <s>dharma</s>- and <s>anvaya</s>-knowledge; one [knows] another in the seeing-moments;
a <s>śrāvaka</s> knows [the minds of] three [types]; a <s>khaḍga</s> (-like <s>pratyekabuddha</s>), three; a <s>Buddha</s>, all—without effort.
The knowledge of destruction is, regarding the truths, the ascertainment 'fully known' (<s>parijñāta</s>) etc.;
the cognition of non-arising is the view 'nothing more to be known' (<s>na parijñeya</s>) etc.
From own-nature and opponent, from aspect and object of aspect,
from practice, accomplished-duty, cause, and accumulation—[there are] ten [knowledges].
That which is <s>dharmajñāna</s> regarding cessation or the path, on the meditation-path,
is the opponent of all three realms; that of the desire realm alone is not <s>anvaya</s> (subsequent).
<s>Dharmajñāna</s> and <s>anvayajñāna</s> have sixteen aspects; the conventional [knowledge] has otherwise;

children.text: tathā ca sāṃvṛtaṃ svaiḥ svaiḥ satyākāraiścatuṣṭayam // VAkK_7.10 //
children.translated_text: and likewise, the conventional [knowledge], with its own aspects of each truth, is fourfold.
Likewise the knowledge of others' minds; the stainless [type] and the stained [type] again
have the aspect of the particular characteristic of the knowable and have a single entity as object.
The remaining [knowledge has] fourteen aspects, excluding emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>) and non-self (<s>anātma</s>);

children.text: nāmalaḥ ṣoḍaśabhyo 'nya ākāraḥ anye 'sti śāstrataḥ // VAkK_7.12 //
children.translated_text: there is no stainless aspect other than the sixteen; other [aspects] exist [only] from the <s>śāstra</s> [perspective].
In substance, the sixteen aspects [are] the wisdom-aspect; together with that [wisdom],

children.text: ākārayanti sālambāḥ sarvamākāryate tu sat // VAkK_7.13 //
children.translated_text: all that has an object gives aspects; but whatever exists is aspectized.
The first [conventional knowledge] is threefold [wholesome, unwholesome, indeterminate]; the others are wholesome; the first [is found] in all stages;

children.text: dharmākhyaṃ ṣaṭsu navasu tvanvayākhyaṃ tathaiva ṣaṭ // VAkK_7.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharmajñāna</s> in six [stages]; <s>anvayajñāna</s> likewise in six; [and those again] in nine.
The knowledge of others' minds [operates] in the <s>dhyānas</s>; its basis is the desire and form realms;
but <s>dharmajñāna</s> has the desire realm as basis; the other [knowledge has] all three realms as basis.
One foundation of mindfulness—cognition regarding cessation; knowledge of others' minds—

children.text: trīṇi catvāri śeṣāṇi dharmadhīgocaro nava // VAkK_7.16 //
children.translated_text: three [foundations]; four [foundations for] the rest; the object of <s>dharmajñāna</s> is nine.
Nine for the path- and subsequent-knowledges; two for the suffering- and cause-knowledges;

children.text: caturṇāṃ daśa naikasya yojyā dharmāḥ punardaśa // VAkK_7.17 //
children.translated_text: ten for the four [remaining]; of a single [knowledge], the dharmas that may be connected are again ten.
The dharmas of the three realms, the stainless, and the unconditioned—each twofold.
The conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) [knowledge] should be known as non-self (<s>anātmataḥ</s>), being one [yet different] from other [dharmas] in its own aggregate. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.18 //
One possessed of attachment, connected with a single knowledge, in the first undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>) moment,
in the second [moment has] three; and above, increasing by one in each of the four [remaining truth-moments]. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.19 //
As the <s>kṣāntis</s> (acceptances) and <s>jñānas</s> (knowledges) that have arisen are cultivated in the path of seeing (<s>darśana</s>),
so too those yet to arise [are cultivated] in that same [path]; and the conventional [knowledge] in the three subsequent [truths]. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.20 //
Therefore, [it is called] the 'final <s>abhisamaya</s>' (comprehension); that [state] has the nature of non-arising (<s>anutpattidharmaka</s>);
regarding cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) of one's own and lower stages, the final [moment] has the aspect of one's own truth; it is effortful (<s>yātnika</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.21 //

children.text: ṣoḍaśe ṣaṭ sarāgasya vītarāgasya sapta tu /
children.translated_text: In the sixteenth [moment], six [knowledges] for one with attachment; seven, however, for one free from attachment;
on the meditation-path (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) for one with attachment, above that—seven [knowledges] are cultivated. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.22 //
in the <s>ānantaryapathas</s> (uninterrupted paths) above, and in the eight liberation-paths (<s>muktimārga</s>) as well— // <s>VAkK</s> 7.23 //

body.translated_text: In the [meditation practices of] conquest of seven stages, <s>abhijñā</s> (supernatural knowledge), <s>akopya</s> (unshakeable) attainment, and mixed (<s>ākīrṇa</s>) cultivation,

children.translated_text: in the learner's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) 'heating' (<s>uttāpana</s>) and liberation, six or seven knowledges are cultivated;
in the uninterrupted path of the six [attainments], and likewise in the conquest of the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>)— // <s>VAkK</s> 7.24 //

children.text: navānāṃ tu kṣayajñāne akopyasya daśa bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: nine [knowledges] in the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayajñāna</s>); for the <s>akopya</s> (unshakeable one), ten [knowledges] are cultivated;
in its repeated attainment (<s>saṃcara</s>) and in the final liberation, eight [knowledges] are cultivated as stated for the remainder. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.25 //
For the sake of detachment from whatever, whatever [knowledge] is attained—there and below it is cultivated;

children.text: sāsravāśca kṣayajñāne labdhapūrvaṃ na bhāvyate // VAkK_7.26 //
children.translated_text: but the defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>) [knowledges] in the knowledge of destruction—[what was] previously obtained is not cultivated. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.26 //
There are [four] cultivations called 'obtainment' (<s>pratilambha</s>) and 'repeated practice' (<s>niṣevā</s>), which are wholesome conditioned (<s>śubhasaṃskṛta</s>) cultivations;
and 'antidote' (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) and 'removal' (<s>vinirdhāva</s>) cultivations—these are of the defiled (<s>sāsrava</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.27 //
The eighteen special (<s>āveṇika</s>) <s>buddhadharmas</s> are the <s>balas</s> (powers) and so forth;

children.text: sthānāsthāne daśa jñānāni aṣṭau karmaphale nava // VAkK_7.28 //
children.translated_text: regarding what is possible and impossible (<s>sthānāsthāna</s>)—ten knowledges; regarding the eight [types of] <s>karmaphala</s> (action-results)—nine. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.28 //
Regarding <s>dhyānas</s> and so forth, sense-bases (<s>akṣa</s>), liberations (<s>adhimokṣa</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and practices (<s>pratipat</s>)—

children.text: daśa vā saṃvṛtijñānaṃ dvayoḥ ṣaṭ daśa vā kṣaye // VAkK_7.29 //
children.translated_text: ten, or conventional knowledge; in the two [powers]—six or ten; in destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>) [knowledge—ten]. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.29 //
In the powers of [knowledge of] the past, rebirth and death, arising, and <s>dhyānas</s>—the remainder [of knowledges];
in all stages—by what [means] is his power unobstructed (<s>avyāhata</s>)? Because— // <s>VAkK</s> 7.30 //
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-power in the body; in the joints, others [say] ten times more;
the power of a group of seven elephants [etc.]; and that is the tangible sense-base (<s>spraṣṭavyāyatana</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.31 //
The <s>vaiśāradya</s> (fearlessness) is fourfold: as in the first [and] the tenth power;
and as in the second [and] the seventh—the [remaining] three are of the nature of mindfulness and wisdom. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.32 //
Great compassion (<s>mahākṛpā</s>) is conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtidhī</s>); by its equipment (<s>saṃbhāra</s>), aspect, and object,
from its equality and intensity, and [from other distinguishing features]—it differs [from ordinary compassion] in eight ways. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.33 //
By equipment and the <s>dharmakāya</s>, and by beneficial activity (<s>arthacaryā</s>) for the world,
[there is] equality of all <s>Buddhas</s>—not by lifespan, birth, or measure. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.34 //
Other dharmas shared with disciples, some [shared even] with ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>)—
<s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict), <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (resolution-knowledge), <s>pratisaṃvid</s> (analytical knowledge), [and other] qualities, etc. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.35 //
<s>Araṇā</s> is conventional knowledge, in the last <s>dhyāna</s>, of one with the <s>akopya</s> (unshakeable) quality;
born among humans, of one who has not produced [defilements in the] desire [realm], one who has obtained [attainment], having defilements as its object. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.36 //

children.text: tathaiva praṇidhijñānaṃ sarvālambaṃ tu tat tathā /
children.translated_text: Likewise the <s>praṇidhijñāna</s> (resolution-knowledge); it has all [dharmas] as its object, and likewise

children.text: dharmārthayorniruktau ca pratibhāne ca saṃvidaḥ // VAkK_7.37 //
children.translated_text: the <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges) concern <s>dharma</s>, meaning (<s>artha</s>), etymology (<s>nirukti</s>), and eloquence (<s>pratibhāna</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.37 //
Three [relate to] name, meaning, speech-knowledge [respectively]; [they are] irreversible (<s>avivartya</s>), in due order;
the fourth is connected with ready speech, [operating in] mastery over designations and paths. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.38 //
And that [fourth, <s>pratibhāna</s>] has speech-paths as its object; nine knowledges, [present] in all stages;

children.text: daśa ṣaḍvārthasaṃvit sā sarvatra anye tu sāṃvṛtam // VAkK_7.39 //
children.translated_text: ten or six—<s>arthasaṃvid</s> (knowledge of meaning) is everywhere; the others, however, are conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.39 //
<s>Dharma</s>-knowledge [operates] in the desire realm and <s>dhyānas</s>; speech-knowledge in the first [dhyāna] and desire realm;
those who are deficient [in faculties] do not attain it; these six are 'frontier-dwellers' (<s>prāntakoṭikāḥ</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.40 //
That [analytical knowledge] is sixfold, conforming to all stages;
and that [which has] reached the peak of growth—for a <s>Buddha</s> it is innate; for others, it arises from practice (<s>prayoga</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.41 //
In <s>ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power), divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), knowledge of others' minds, former births, death-and-rebirth, and destruction [of defilements]—

children.text: jñāta sākṣīkriyābhijñā ṣaḍ vidhā muktimārgadhīḥ // VAkK_7.42 //
children.translated_text: these are known, directly witnessed; the six <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges) are of the nature of liberation-path knowledge. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.42 //
Four are conventional knowledge; knowledge of others' minds is fivefold knowledge;

children.text: kṣayābhijñā balaṃ yadvat pañca dhyānacatuṣṭaye // VAkK_7.43 //
children.translated_text: the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣayābhijñā</s>) is like the [ten] powers; the five [abhijñās] are in the four <s>dhyānas</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.43 //
They have their own and lower stages as domain; [they are] obtained from detachment; but the proper [domains]—
the third [abhijñā has] three foundations of mindfulness; the first [has] the ear, <s>ṛddhi</s> [has] the eye [as basis]. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.44 //
The divine ear and eye <s>abhijñās</s> are indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>); the others are wholesome;

children.text: tisro vidyāḥ avidyāyāḥ pūrvāntādau nivarttanāt // VAkK_7.45 //
children.translated_text: three [are called] <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges)—because they remove <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) regarding the past and so forth. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.45 //
The last [vidyā belongs to] a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>); two are called by that name, because they arise from his continuum;

children.text: iṣṭe śaikṣasya nokte tu vidye sāvidyasaṃtateḥ // VAkK_7.46 //
children.translated_text: for a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), [the last two] are accepted but not called <s>vidyā</s>, because [they arise from] a continuum with <s>avidyā</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.46 //

children.text: ādyā tṛtīyā ṣaṣṭhī ca prātihāryāṇi śāsanam /
children.translated_text: The first, third, and sixth [abhijñās are] the [three] miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>); the teaching [miracle is]
supreme, because it is unfailing and because it connects what is desired with its fruit. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.47 //

children.text: ṛddhiḥ samādhiḥ gamanaṃ nirmāṇaṃ ca gatistridhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛddhi</s> (supernatural power) is <s>samādhi</s>; travel and creation (<s>nirmāṇa</s>)—travel is threefold;
for the Teacher, [it is] mind-swift (<s>manojava</s>); for others, like a flowing stream; also through <s>adhimokṣa</s> (resolve). // <s>VAkK</s> 7.48 //
What is obtained in the desire realm—a creation, external, of the four sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>), twofold;

children.text: rūpāptaṃ dve tu nirmāṇacittaistāni caturdaśa // VAkK_7.49 //
children.translated_text: form obtained—two; but with creation-minds, those are fourteen. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.49 //

children.text: yathākramaṃ dhyānaphalaṃ dve yāvat pañca nordhvajam /
children.translated_text: In order, the fruit of [each] <s>dhyāna</s>: two up to five; not of the upper [formless realm];

children.text: tallābho dhyānavat śuddhāttatsvataśca tato 'pi te // VAkK_7.50 //
children.translated_text: the attainment of that is like <s>dhyāna</s>—from the pure [realm], from itself, and from that also [come] those. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.50 //
Creation is by [a mind] of one's own stage; but speech is by a lower [mind] as well;
the creator alone [is active] together with [those of] the Teacher; [the creations continue] by sustained intention (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>), without other activity. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.51 //
Even for one who has died, there is sustained intention (<s>adhiṣṭhāna</s>)—not for one who is unstable; but others [say] no;
at first, one [creation] by many [minds]; but when mastered, the reverse. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.52 //
Indeterminate (<s>avyākṛta</s>), born from cultivation—threefold; but that born from rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>),

children.text: ṛddhirmantrauṣadhābhyāṃ ca karmajā ceti pañcadhā // VAkK_7.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>ṛddhi</s> from mantras and herbs, and that born from <s>karma</s>—thus fivefold. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.53 //
The divine ear and eye are refinements (<s>prasāda</s>) of form, of the <s>dhyāna</s>-stage;
[they are] <s>sabhāga</s> (homogeneous), not deficient, always [operating] in the domain of what is distant, subtle, etc. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.54 //
The fleshly eye does not see what is distant, obstructed, subtle, or [in] all [directions]—because form [is limited];
therefore the divine eye is desired [for seeing what the fleshly eye cannot]. //
An <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>khaḍga</s> (-like <s>pratyekabuddha</s>), and a Guide [see across] two, three, or countless thousand-world-systems;
others too [see through that] obtained by rebirth; the intermediate being (<s>antarābhava</s>) is not [an object] visible to that. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.55 //

children.text: cetojñānaṃ tu tattredhā tarkavidyākṛtaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of others' minds (<s>cetojñāna</s>) is threefold—that which is produced by inference (<s>tarka</s>) and learning (<s>vidyā</s>);

children.text: jānate nārakā ādau nṛṇāṃ notpattilabhikam // VAkK_7.56 //
children.translated_text: hell-beings and others in the beginning know [minds of others]; [but] that obtained at birth among humans [does] not. // <s>VAkK</s> 7.56 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, entitled 'Exposition on Knowledge' (<s>Jñānanirdeśa</s>). //

children.translated_text: The four <s>dhyānas</s> are said to be twofold; their [corresponding] rebirths (<s>upapatti</s>) [are likewise];
<s>samāpatti</s> (attainment) is wholesome one-pointedness (<s>śubhaikāgra</s>); [it consists of] five <s>skandhas</s>, together with their accompaniments. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.1 //
Possessing investigation (<s>vicāra</s>), joy (<s>prīti</s>), and bliss (<s>sukha</s>); [each subsequent dhyāna] lacks the preceding members, one by one;
likewise the formless [attainments] are four-<s>skandha</s> [aggregates]; they arise from separation from the lower stage. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.2 //
They are called 'having transcended form and perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>)'; together with the three <s>sāmantakas</s> (preliminary stages)—
in the formless [realm] there is no [actual] existence of form; but form arises [again] from mind. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.3 //
They are designated as [meditations on] infinite space (<s>ākāśānantya</s>), infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantya</s>), nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanya</s>),
and so named from their respective practices; but due to sluggishness, [the fourth is] 'neither-perception-nor-non-perception' (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñā</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.4 //
Thus the fundamental (<s>maula</s>) attainment-substance is eightfold [and] threefold:
seven are [either] savoring (<s>āsvādana</s>), pure (<s>śuddha</s>), or undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>); the eighth is twofold. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.5 //
That associated with savoring (<s>āsvādana</s>), accompanied by craving, worldly and wholesome,
is the pure (<s>śuddhaka</s>); that [which is] tasted by each [is savoring]; the supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>) is undefiled (<s>anāsrava</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.6 //
In the first [dhyāna], five members: <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought), <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), <s>prīti</s> (joy), <s>sukha</s> (bliss), and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration);
in the second, four members: <s>prīti</s> and so forth, and faith (<s>prasāda</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.7 //

children.text: tṛtīye pañca tūpekṣā smṛtiḥ prajñā sukhaṃ sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: In the third, five: equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), bliss (<s>sukha</s>), and concentration (<s>sthiti</s>);
in the last [dhyāna], four: neither-pleasure-nor-pain (<s>asukhāduḥkha</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), and <s>samādhi</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.8 //

children.text: dravyato daśa caikaṃ ca prasrabdhi sukhamādyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: In substance, [there are] ten plus one; tranquility (<s>prasrabdhi</s>) [equals] bliss in the first two [dhyānas];

children.text: śraddhā prasādaḥ prītistu saumanasyaṃ dvidhāgamāt // VAkK_8.9 //
children.translated_text: faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) is 'clarity' (<s>prasāda</s>); but <s>prīti</s> (joy) is mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>)—twofold according to scripture. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.9 //
In the defiled [dhyānas], there is neither joy nor bliss, [but there is] clarity, discernment (<s>saṃpradhī</s>), mindfulness,
purity of equanimity and mindfulness; some [include] tranquility and equanimity. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.10 //
Because it is freed from the eight defects (<s>apakṣāla</s>), the fourth [dhyāna] is called 'immovable' (<s>āniñja</s>);

children.text: vitarkacārau śvāsau ca sukhādi ca catuṣṭayam // VAkK_8.11 //
children.translated_text: [those eight are:] <s>vitarka</s>, <s>vicāra</s>, the two breathings (<s>śvāsa</s>), and the four [consisting of] bliss, etc. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.11 //
Mental pleasure (<s>saumanasya</s>), bliss (<s>sukha</s>), equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>)—[respectively in] equanimity and mental displeasure,
bliss and equanimity, equanimity—[these are] the feelings in the <s>dhyāna</s>-rebirths. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.12 //
The body, eye, and ear consciousnesses, and that which generates bodily and vocal expression (<s>vijñapti</s>)—

children.text: dvitīyādau tadādyāptaṃ akliṣṭāvyākṛtaṃ ca tat // VAkK_8.13 //
children.translated_text: [these are present] from the second [dhyāna] onward; from the first [dhyāna] onward; and they are undefiled-indeterminate (<s>akliṣṭāvyākṛta</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.13 //
One who lacks it obtains the pure [attainment] through detachment and by way of rebirth;

children.text: anāsravaṃ tu vairāgyāt kliṣṭaṃ hānyupapattitaḥ // VAkK_8.14 //
children.translated_text: the undefiled, however, [is attained] through detachment; the defiled, through deterioration (<s>hāni</s>) and rebirth. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.14 //
From the third [dhyāna] upward, [and] from the undefiled immediately [below], the wholesome [attainment]

children.text: utpadyate tathā śuddhāt kliṭaṃ cāpi svabhūmikam // VAkK_8.15 //
children.translated_text: arises; likewise from the pure; and the defiled also of one's own stage. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.15 //

children.text: kliṣṭāt svaṃ śuddakaṃ kliṣṭaṃ evaṃ cādharaśuddhakam /
children.translated_text: From the defiled [arises] one's own pure or defiled, and likewise the lower pure;

children.text: cyutau tu śuddhakāt kliṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ kliṣṭāttu nottaram // VAkK_8.16 //
children.translated_text: but at death (<s>cyuti</s>), from the pure [arises] the defiled; everything from the defiled—but not a higher [one]. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.16 //
The pure [attainment] is fourfold: 'deterioration-part' (<s>hānabhāgīya</s>) and so forth, in due order;
conforming respectively to defilement-arising, one's own stage, the higher [stage], and the undefiled. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.17 //

children.text: dve trīṇi trīṇi caikaṃ ca hāna bhāgādyanantaram /
children.translated_text: Two, three, three, and one—[these are] what immediately follow the deterioration-part, etc.;

children.text: gatvāgamya dvidhā bhūmīraṣṭau śliṣṭai kalaṅghitāḥ // VAkK_8.18 //
children.translated_text: after going, returning, [there are] eight stages in two [modes]—connected and leapt-over (<s>kalaṅghita</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.18 //
The 'skip-attainment' (<s>vyutkrāntakasamāpatti</s>) goes to the dissimilar [and] the third [stage];
the <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments] have only their own and lower stages as basis; [it would be] useless otherwise. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.19 //
Because a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) [who is] near to <s>ākiṃcanya</s> [can destroy defilements] at the peak of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>), the destruction of defilements [occurs there];

children.text: satṛṣṇāḥ svabhavālambāḥ dhyānaṃ sadviṣayaṃ śubham // VAkK_8.20 //
children.translated_text: accompanied by craving, having their own existence as object—<s>dhyāna</s>, when wholesome, has a [good] domain. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.20 //
The fundamental wholesome formless [attainments] do not have a lower [stage] as object while defiled;

children.text: anāsraveṇa hīyante kleśāḥ sāmantakena ca // VAkK_8.21 //
children.translated_text: by the undefiled, defilements are abandoned; and by the <s>sāmantaka</s> (preliminary stage) also. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.21 //
The eight <s>sāmantakas</s> (preliminary stages) of these [dhyānas]—the pure [ones] are [with] neither-pleasure-nor-pain;

children.text: ārya cādyaṃ tridhā kecit atarka dhyānamantaram // VAkK_8.22 //
children.translated_text: the first, for a noble one, is threefold; some [say] the intermediate <s>dhyāna</s> is without <s>vitarka</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.22 //
The 'neither-pleasure-nor-pain' is threefold; and that [third dhyāna of this type] is the <s>Mahābrahmā</s> fruit;
below is <s>samādhi</s> with <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>; beyond that, [samādhi] without both. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.23 //
<s>Ānimitta</s> (signless [samādhi]) operates with the aspects of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), non-self (<s>anātma</s>), and [pure] emptiness;
<s>apraṇihita</s> (wishless [samādhi operates]) with the aspects of the truths; beyond those— // <s>VAkK</s> 8.24 //
the pure and stainless [concentrations]; but the immaculate (<s>nirmala</s>) ones are the threefold liberation-gate (<s>vimokṣamukha</s>);
the three called 'emptiness of emptiness' (<s>śūnyatāśūnyatā</s>) etc. are the 'other' <s>samādhis</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.25 //
