Two take the non-learner's [dharmas] as object; and 'emptiness of emptiness' [takes] impermanence;
'signless of the signless' (<s>ānimittānimitta</s>) [takes] cessation; [these arise] by the incalculable [method] in the knowledge of destruction (<s>kṣaya</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.26 //
They are defiled, [and arise] among humans; for the <s>akopya</s> (unshakeable one), the seven <s>sāmantakas</s> are excluded;

children.text: samādhibhāvanā dhyānaṃ subhamādyaṃ sukhāya hi // VAkK_8.27 //
children.translated_text: the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> [includes] the <s>dhyāna</s>—the first wholesome [dhyāna] is for the sake of happiness. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.27 //

For the sake of vision (<s>darśana</s>), [for obtaining] the <s>abhijñās</s> (supernatural knowledges)—[these are] desired; for the sake of discriminating knowledge (<s>dhībheda</s>), they arise from practice;
the diamond-like (<s>vajropama</s>) [samādhi], in the final <s>dhyāna</s>, [is] the cultivation for the destruction of the defiled. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.28 //
The four <s>apramāṇas</s> (immeasurables) [are] antidotes to ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>) and so forth;

children.text: maitryadveṣaḥ api karuṇā muditā sumanaskatā // VAkK_8.29 //
children.translated_text: <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) [opposes] hatred; compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), [likewise]; sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) [relates to] mental pleasure (<s>sumanaskatā</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.29 //
Equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) [opposes] attachment (<s>lobha</s>); the aspects [are]: 'May they be happy,' 'How they suffer!'
'May they rejoice!'—and beings [are the object]; but the domain is beings in the desire realm. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.30 //

children.text: dhyānayormuditā anyāni ṣaṭ su kecittu pañcasu /
children.translated_text: Sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>) [operates] in two <s>dhyānas</s>; the others in six [stages]; but some [say] in five;

children.text: na taiḥ prahāṇaṃ nṛṣveva janyante tryanvito dhruvam // VAkK_8.31 //
children.translated_text: there is no abandonment by them; they are produced among humans alone; one always possesses three. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.31 //
The eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations): the first two [are the] <s>aśubha</s> (impurity [contemplations]) in the two <s>dhyānas</s>;

children.text: tṛtīyo 'ntye sa cālobhaḥ śubhārūpyāḥ samāhitāḥ // VAkK_8.32 //
children.translated_text: the third is in the last [dhyāna]; and it is non-attachment (<s>alobha</s>); the pure and formless [liberations] are [states of] absorption (<s>samāhita</s>). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.32 //
<s>Nirodha</s> (cessation) is [also] an attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>); immediately after the subtlest of the subtle [mental states],
[it is attained] from one's own pure [stage]; by a noble one; emergence (<s>vyutthāna</s>) [is] then by that mind. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.33 //
The first [liberations] have objects visible and obtained in the desire realm; but those who are formless—
they [pertain to] the subsequent knowledge (<s>anvayajñāna</s>) side, [with] the higher stages and one's own stage [as domain for] suffering etc. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.34 //
The eight <s>abhibhvāyatanas</s> (bases of mastery)—two [are] like the first <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation);

children.text: dve dvitīyavat anyāni punaḥ śubhavimokṣavat // VAkK_8.35 //
children.translated_text: Two [are] like the second; the others, again, are like the <s>śubhavimokṣa</s> (pure liberation). // <s>VAkK</s> 8.35 //

children.text: daśa kṛtsnāni alobhāṣṭau dhyāne 'ntye gocaraḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: The ten <s>kṛtsnāyatanas</s> (totalities) — eight [pertain to] non-attachment; in the last <s>dhyāna</s>, moreover, [is] the domain,
Two [are in] the desire [realm], [two in] the pure [dhyānas]; in the formless realm, [they have] their own four-<s>skandha</s> domain. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.36 //
<s>Nirodha</s> (cessation) has been explained. What is obtained through <s>vairāgya</s> (detachment) and <s>prayoga</s> (practice), however, is the remainder,
Based on the three realms, the formless [attainments] are so designated; the remainder is born among humans. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.37 //
The production of the formless [attainments] in two realms [is] through cause, <s>karma</s> (action), and innate power,

children.text: dhyānānāṃ rūpadhātau tu tābhyāṃ dharmatayāpi ca // VAkK_8.38 //
children.translated_text: But the production of the <s>dhyānas</s> in the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) [is] through those two and also through the nature of <s>dharmas</s>. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.38 //
The true <s>Dharma</s> of the Teacher is twofold, consisting of <s>āgama</s> (scriptural tradition) and <s>adhigama</s> (realization),

children.text: dhātārastasya vaktāraḥ pratipattāra eva ca // VAkK_8.39 //
children.translated_text: Its supporters are the expounders and the practitioners themselves. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.39 //
This <s>Abhidharma</s> has been expounded by me mostly in accordance with the established doctrine of the <s>Kāśmīra</s> <s>Vaibhāṣikas</s>,

children.text: yaddurguhītaṃ tadihāsmadāgaḥ saddharmanītau munayaḥ pramāṇam // VAkK_8.40 //
children.translated_text: Whatever has been poorly grasped herein is my fault; in matters of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the sages are the authority. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.40 //

children.text: nimīlite śāstari lokacakṣuṣi kṣayaṃ gate sākṣijane ca bhūyasā /
children.translated_text: When the Teacher, the eye of the world, has closed [his eyes], and when the witnesses have for the most part perished,
This teaching has been thrown into confusion by false logicians who have not seen the truth, who are without restraint. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.41 //

children.text: gate 'tha śāntiṃ paramāṃ svayaṃbhuvi svayaṃbhuvaḥ śāsanadhūrdhareṣu ca /
children.translated_text: Now that the Self-Arisen One has gone to supreme peace, and those who bore the yoke of the Self-Arisen One's teaching [have also gone],

children.text: jagatyanāthe gaṇaghātibhirmataiḥ niraṅkuśaiḥ svairamihādya caryate // VAkK_8.42 //
children.translated_text: In this unprotected world, those whose views destroy the <s>saṅgha</s> now wander freely, unchecked. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.42 //
Thus, knowing that the Sage's teaching has its life-breath at the throat,

children.text: balakālaṃ malānāṃ ca na pramādyaṃ mumukṣubhiḥ // VAkK_8.43 //
children.translated_text: And [knowing] the strength and timing of the defilements, those who seek liberation must not be negligent. // <s>VAkK</s> 8.43 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter of the <s>Abhidharmakośa</s>, entitled 'Exposition on Attainments' (<s>Samāpattinirdeśa</s>). //
